sentences.zh: =魏紀四=

translations.literal: = Wei Records 4 =
translations.idiomatic: Wei Records 4

sentences.zh: 起重光大淵獻，盡閼逢攝提格，凡四年。

translations.literal: Beginning with Zhongguang Dayuanxian, ending with Yanfeng Shetige, four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Spanning from the year Zhongguang Dayuanxian through Yanfeng Shetige—a period of four years.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝中之上

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, middle scroll, upper part.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Two (beginning)

sentences.zh: 1春，二月，吳主假太常潘濬節，使與呂岱督諸軍五萬人討五溪蠻。

translations.literal: 1. Spring, second month, the Lord of Wu lent Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan Jun his staff of authority and ordered him, together with Lü Dai, to command an army of fifty thousand to suppress the Five Streams barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, during the second month, Sun Quan lent Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan Jun his staff of authority and ordered him, together with Lü Dai, to lead fifty thousand troops against the Five Streams tribes.

sentences.zh: 濬姨兄蔣琬為諸葛亮長史，武陵太守衛旍奏濬遣密使與琬相聞，欲有自託之計。

translations.literal: Jun's cousin on his mother's side, Jiang Wan, was Zhuge Liang's chief clerk; Wuling Administrator Wei Zheng memorialized that Jun had sent secret envoys to communicate with Wan, intending a plan to entrust himself to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's maternal cousin Jiang Wan served as Zhuge Liang's chief clerk. The administrator of Wuling, Wei Zheng, reported that Jun had sent secret messengers to contact Wan, evidently hoping to place himself under Shu's protection.

sentences.zh: 吳主曰：「承明不為此也。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu said, "Chengming would not do such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said, "Chengming would never do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 」即封旍表以示濬，而召旍還，免官。

translations.literal: " He immediately sealed Zheng's memorial and showed it to Jun, then summoned Zheng back and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: " He at once sealed up Zheng's memorial and showed it to Jun, then recalled Zheng and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 2衛溫、諸葛直軍行經歲，士卒疾疫死者什八九，亶洲絕遠，卒不可得至，得夷洲數千人還。

translations.literal: 2. Wei Wen and Zhuge Zhi's expedition had been underway for a year; eight or nine tenths of the soldiers died of epidemic illness. Danzhou was impossibly remote and could not be reached in the end; they brought back several thousand men from Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Wei Wen and Zhuge Zhi had been at sea for a year, and eight or nine soldiers in ten succumbed to disease. Danzhou proved too distant to reach; in the end they returned with several thousand captives from Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 溫、直坐無功，誅。

translations.literal: Wen and Zhi were punished for achieving nothing and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Zhi were condemned for their failure and put to death.

sentences.zh: 3漢丞相亮命李嚴以中都護署府事。

translations.literal: 3. Han Chancellor Liang ordered Li Yan to act as Central Supervisor of the Army and manage affairs at headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: 3. Zhuge Liang, chancellor of Han, appointed Li Yan Central Supervisor of the Army to administer headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 嚴更名平。

translations.literal: Yan changed his name to Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Yan changed his personal name to Ping.

sentences.zh: 亮帥諸軍入寇，圍祁山，以木牛運。

translations.literal: Liang led the armies in an incursion, besieged Qishan, and used wooden oxen for transport.
translations.idiomatic: Liang led his forces north, laid siege to Qishan, and supplied them with his wooden-ox transport.

sentences.zh: 於是大司馬曹真有疾，帝命司馬懿西屯長安，督將軍張郃、費曜、戴陵、郭淮等以禦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Marshal Cao Zhen fell ill, and the emperor ordered Sima Yi to encamp west at Chang'an and supervise Generals Zhang He, Fei Yao, Dai Ling, Guo Huai, and others to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Cao Zhen had fallen ill, so the emperor ordered Sima Yi to take up position at Chang'an and direct Generals Zhang He, Fei Yao, Dai Ling, Guo Huai, and others against the invasion.

sentences.zh: 4三月，邵陵元侯曹真卒。

translations.literal: 4. Third month, Marquis Yuan of Shaoling, Cao Zhen, died.
translations.idiomatic: 4. In the third month, Cao Zhen, Marquis Yuan of Shaoling, died.

sentences.zh: 5自十月不雨，至于是月。

translations.literal: 5. From the tenth month there had been no rain, until this month.
translations.idiomatic: 5. No rain had fallen since the tenth month, and the drought continued into this month.

sentences.zh: 6司馬懿使費曜、戴陵留精兵四千守上邽，餘眾悉出，西救祁山。

translations.literal: 6. Sima Yi had Fei Yao and Dai Ling leave four thousand picked troops to hold Shanggui and led the rest out west to relieve Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: 6. Sima Yi left Fei Yao and Dai Ling with four thousand elite troops to hold Shanggui and marched west with the rest of his force to relieve Qishan.

sentences.zh: 張郃欲分兵駐雍、郿，懿曰：「料前軍能獨當之者，將軍言是也。

translations.literal: Zhang He wished to detach troops to garrison Yong and Mei. Yi said, "If you judge that the vanguard can hold its own alone, General, you are right.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He wanted to detach troops to garrison Yong and Mei. Yi replied, "If you believe the vanguard can hold on its own, General, you are right.

sentences.zh: 若不能當而分為前後，此楚之三軍所以為黥布禽也。

translations.literal: But if they cannot hold and you split into front and rear, that is why the three armies of Chu were captured by Qing Bu."
translations.idiomatic: But if they cannot hold and you divide into front and rear, you will repeat how the three armies of Chu were taken by Qing Bu."

sentences.zh: 」遂進。

translations.literal: " He thereupon advanced.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 亮分兵留攻祁山，自逆懿於上邽。

translations.literal: Liang divided his forces, leaving part to press the attack on Qishan, and himself went to meet Yi at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Liang detached troops to continue the siege of Qishan and marched in person to confront Yi at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 郭淮、費曜等徼亮，亮破之，因大芟刈其麥，與懿遇於上邽之東。

translations.literal: Guo Huai, Fei Yao, and others intercepted Liang; Liang defeated them and thereupon reaped their wheat in great quantities, then encountered Yi east of Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai, Fei Yao, and others tried to intercept Liang, but he routed them and then reaped the wheat fields in force before meeting Yi east of Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 懿斂軍依險，兵不得交，亮引還。

translations.literal: Yi drew up his army in difficult terrain so that the forces could not engage; Liang withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yi drew up his army on difficult ground so that neither side could close; Liang then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 懿等尋亮後至于鹵城。

translations.literal: Yi and the others followed after Liang and reached Lucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi pursued Liang as far as Lucheng.

sentences.zh: 張郃曰：「彼遠來逆我，請戰不得，謂我利不在戰，欲以長計制之也。

translations.literal: Zhang He said, "They came from afar to meet us and could not obtain battle; they will think our interest lies not in fighting and that we intend to wear them down with a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He said, "They marched far to meet us and could not get us to fight; they will conclude we do not want battle and mean to wear them down over time.

sentences.zh: 且祁山知大軍已在近，人情自固，可止屯於此，分為奇兵，示出其後，不宜進前而不敢逼，坐失民望也。

translations.literal: Moreover, once Qishan knows the great army is near, morale there will steady itself. We can halt and encamp here, detach a flanking force to show ourselves in their rear, and should not advance yet refuse to press them—thus sitting by and losing the people's confidence."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, once Qishan learns the main army is near, its defenders will take heart. We should halt here, send a flanking force to threaten their rear, and not march up only to hang back—that would forfeit the army's confidence."

sentences.zh: 今亮孤軍食少，亦行去矣。

translations.literal: Now Liang is a lone army with little grain; he too will soon depart."
translations.idiomatic: Liang is isolated and short of food; he will withdraw before long."

sentences.zh: 」懿不從，故尋亮。

translations.literal: " Yi did not follow this advice and therefore pursued Liang.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi refused and kept following Liang.

sentences.zh: 既至，又登山掘營，不肯戰。

translations.literal: When they arrived, they again climbed the hills and dug camps, refusing battle.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival they again took the high ground and dug in, still refusing to fight.

sentences.zh: 賈栩、魏平數請戰，因曰：「公畏蜀如虎，奈天下笑何！

translations.literal: Jia Xu and Wei Ping repeatedly asked for battle, saying, "My lord, you fear Shu as one fears a tiger—how will you answer when the world laughs!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu and Wei Ping pressed repeatedly for battle, saying, "You fear Shu as though it were a tiger—what will you say when the world mocks you?"

sentences.zh: 」懿病之。

translations.literal: " Yi was vexed by this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi was deeply annoyed.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸請戰。

translations.literal: All the generals asked for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Every general clamored for battle.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，辛已，懿乃使張郃攻無當監何平於南圍，自案中道向亮。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day Xinsi, Yi then sent Zhang He to attack Supervisor of the Unconquered He Ping at the southern enclosure while he himself advanced on Liang by the middle road.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on the day Xinsi, Yi sent Zhang He against Supervisor of the Unconquered He Ping at the southern camp and marched on Liang himself along the central route.

sentences.zh: 亮使魏延、高翔、吳班逆戰，魏兵大敗，漢人獲甲著三千，懿還保營。

translations.literal: Liang sent Wei Yan, Gao Xiang, and Wu Ban to meet them in battle; the Wei army was utterly defeated, and the Han forces took three thousand suits of armor; Yi retreated to hold his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Wei Yan, Gao Xiang, and Wu Ban to meet the attack; the Wei forces were routed, and the Han army captured three thousand suits of armor. Yi fell back to his camp.

sentences.zh: 六月，亮以糧盡退軍，司馬懿遣張郃追之，〔郃曰：「軍法，圍城必開出路，歸軍勿追。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Liang withdrew for lack of grain; Sima Yi sent Zhang He in pursuit. [He said, "By military law, when you besiege a city you must leave an escape route; do not pursue a returning army."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Liang withdrew for lack of supplies; Sima Yi sent Zhang He in pursuit. [He said, "Military law requires that a besieged city be left an escape route and that a retreating army not be pursued."

sentences.zh: 」懿不聽。

translations.literal: " Yi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 7秋，七月，乙酉，皇子殷生，大赦。

translations.literal: 7. Autumn, seventh month, day Yiyou, the imperial son Yin was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Yiyou, the prince Yin was born and a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 8黃初以來，諸侯王法禁嚴切。

translations.literal: 8. Since the Huangchu era, the laws restraining feudal princes had been severe.
translations.idiomatic: 8. Since the Huangchu era, the laws governing feudal princes had grown harsh.

sentences.zh: 〔吏察之急〕<ref>〔吏察之急〕據章注補。

translations.literal: [Official scrutiny was pressing]<ref>[Official scrutiny was pressing] supplied according to Zhang's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: [Official scrutiny was relentless]<ref>Supplied according to Zhang's commentary.

sentences.zh: </ref>，至于親姻皆不敢相通問。

translations.literal: </ref>, so that even close kin dared not exchange visits.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, until even close kin dared not visit one another.

sentences.zh: 東阿王植上疏曰：「堯之為教，先親後疏，自近及遠。

translations.literal: Prince of Dong'e Zhi submitted a memorial saying, "In Yao's teaching, kin came before the distant, the near before the far.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi, Prince of Dong'e, submitted a memorial: "Yao taught that one should honor kin before strangers, the near before the far.

sentences.zh: 周文王刑于寡妻，至于兄弟，以御于家邦。

translations.literal: King Wen of Zhou began with discipline in his humble wife's quarters, extended it to his brothers, and thereby governed family and state.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou began by disciplining himself before his humble wife, extended that example to his brothers, and so governed both family and realm.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下資帝唐欽明之德，體文王翼翼之仁，惠洽椒房，恩昭九族，群後百寮，番休遞上，執政不廢於公朝，下情得展示私室，親理之路通，慶吊之情展，誠可謂恕己治人，推惠施恩者矣。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty possesses the reverent brilliance of Yao and Shun, embodies King Wen's cautious benevolence, extends grace to the inner palace, makes kindness shine upon the nine degrees of kin, and that the feudal lords and hundred officials rotate in attendance without neglecting public governance, while private sentiments may be shown in the home—family ties are open, congratulations and condolences may be expressed. Truly this may be called governing others by forgiving oneself and spreading favor and grace.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty possesses the reverent brilliance of Yao and Shun, embodies King Wen's cautious benevolence, extends grace to the inner palace, and makes kindness shine upon the nine degrees of kin. The feudal lords and hundred officials rotate in attendance without neglecting public business, while private feelings may still be shown at home—family ties are open, congratulations and condolences may be exchanged. This truly may be called governing others by forgiving oneself and spreading favor and grace.

sentences.zh: 至於臣者，人道絕緒，禁錮明時，臣竊自傷也。

translations.literal: As for me, the way of human relations is cut off; I am confined in this enlightened age, and I grieve in private.
translations.idiomatic: As for me, the bonds of human society are severed; I am confined in this enlightened age, and I grieve in secret.

sentences.zh: 不敢乃望交氣類，修人事，敘人倫。

translations.literal: I dare not even hope to mingle with those of like spirit, cultivate human affairs, or set human relations in order.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not even hope to mingle with kindred spirits, cultivate human affairs, or put human relations in order.

sentences.zh: 近且婚媾不通，兄弟乖絕，吉凶之問塞，慶吊之禮廢。

translations.literal: Lately even marriage alliances are cut off, brothers are estranged, inquiries after good or ill fortune are blocked, and the rites of congratulation and condolence are abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Of late even marriage ties are severed, brothers are estranged, inquiries after good or ill fortune are blocked, and the rites of congratulation and condolence have lapsed.

sentences.zh: 恩紀之違，甚於路人；

translations.literal: The breach of bonds of grace is worse than with strangers in the road;
translations.idiomatic: The breach of bonds of grace is worse than with strangers on the road;

sentences.zh: 隔閡之異，殊於胡越。

translations.literal: the estrangement of separation is more extreme than between Hu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: the estrangement of separation is more extreme than between Hu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 今臣以一切之制，永無朝覲之望，至於注心皇極，結情紫闥，神明知之矣。

translations.literal: Now, under these blanket restrictions, I have forever lost hope of audience at court; yet as for fixing my heart on the imperial pole and binding my feelings to the purple gates, the divine and the bright know this.
translations.idiomatic: Under these blanket restrictions I have forever lost hope of audience at court; yet my heart is fixed on the throne and my feelings bound to the palace gates—the divine powers know this.

sentences.zh: 然天實為之，謂之何哉！

translations.literal: Yet Heaven truly did this—what can one say!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven truly ordained this—what can one say!

sentences.zh: 退惟諸王常有戚戚具爾之心，願陛下沛然垂詔，使諸國慶問，四節得展，以敘骨肉之歡恩，全怡怡之篤義。

translations.literal: Reflecting in retirement, the princes often harbor anxious, earnest hearts; I pray Your Majesty will issue a sweeping edict so that the feudal states may exchange congratulations and inquiries, the four seasons may be observed, kinship's joyful grace may be renewed, and cordial, steadfast righteousness be made whole.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting in retirement, I know the princes often harbor anxious, earnest hearts. I pray Your Majesty will issue a sweeping edict so that the feudal states may exchange congratulations and inquiries, the four seasons may be observed, kinship's joyful grace may be renewed, and cordial, steadfast righteousness made whole.

sentences.zh: 妃妾之家，膏沐之遺，歲得再通，齊義於貴宗，等惠於百司。

translations.literal: The households of consorts and concubines might receive gifts of toilet goods twice a year, equal in propriety to the noble clans and equal in grace to the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: The households of consorts and concubines might receive gifts of toilet goods twice a year, equal in propriety to the noble clans and equal in grace to the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 如此，則古人之所歎，風雅之所詠，復存於聖世矣！

translations.literal: If this were so, what the ancients sighed over and what the Songs and Odes celebrate would again exist in this sage age!
translations.idiomatic: Then what the ancients sighed over and what the Songs and Odes celebrate would live again in this sage age!

sentences.zh: 臣伏自惟省，無錐刀之用；

translations.literal: I humbly reflect upon myself and find no use even for the point of a knife;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect upon myself and find no use even for the point of a knife;

sentences.zh: 及觀陛下之所拔授，若以臣為異姓，竊自料度，不後於朝士矣。

translations.literal: yet observing those Your Majesty promotes and appoints, if I were treated as one of another surname, I venture to judge that I would not rank behind court officials.
translations.idiomatic: yet observing those Your Majesty promotes and appoints, if I were treated as one of another surname, I venture to judge that I would not rank behind court officials.

sentences.zh: 若得辭遠遊，戴武弁，解朱組，佩青紱，駙馬、奉車，趣得一號，安宅京室，執鞭珥筆，出從華蓋，入侍輦轂，承答聖問，拾遺左右，乃臣丹誠之至願，不離於夢想者也。

translations.literal: If I could leave distant wanderings, wear the military cap, lay aside the crimson sash, wear the blue ribbon, serve as Master of the Sidecar or Bearer of the Carriage, obtain some modest title, dwell securely in the capital, hold the whip and wear the writing tablet, go out following the ornate canopy and enter to attend the imperial carriage, answer the sage's questions and gather what others omit at Your side—that would be the utmost wish of my red sincerity, never absent from my dreams.
translations.idiomatic: If I could leave distant exile, wear the military cap, lay aside the crimson sash, wear the blue ribbon, serve as Master of the Sidecar or Bearer of the Carriage, obtain some modest title, dwell securely in the capital, hold the whip and wear the writing tablet, go out following the ornate canopy and enter to attend the imperial carriage, answer Your questions and gather what others omit at Your side—that would be the utmost wish of my loyal heart, never absent from my dreams.

sentences.zh: 遠慕《鹿鳴》君臣之宴，中詠《常棣》匪他之誡，不思《伐木》友生之義，終懷《蓼莪》罔極之哀。

translations.literal: From afar I admire the lord-and-minister feast of "Deer Cry"; within I chant the admonition of "Cherry-apple" that kin are not other; I do not think of the friendship of "Felling Trees"; I end by cherishing the boundless grief of "Smartweed-Eulalia."
translations.idiomatic: From afar I admire the lord-and-minister feast of "Deer Cry"; within I chant the admonition of "Cherry-apple" that kin are not other; I do not think of the friendship of "Felling Trees"; I end by cherishing the boundless grief of "Smartweed-Eulalia."

sentences.zh: 每四節之會，塊然獨處，左右惟僕隸，所對惟妻子，高談無所與陳，精義無所與展，未嘗不聞樂而拊心，臨觴而歎息也。

translations.literal: At each gathering of the four seasons I sit alone in isolation; at my side are only servants, my only companions my wife and children; there is no one with whom to unfold lofty discourse or refine meaning. Never have I heard music without striking my breast, or faced a cup without sighing.
translations.idiomatic: At each gathering of the four seasons I sit alone in isolation; at my side are only servants, my only companions my wife and children; there is no one with whom to unfold lofty discourse or refine meaning. Never have I heard music without striking my breast, or faced a cup without sighing.

sentences.zh: 臣伏以犬馬之誠不能動人，譬人之誠不能動天，崩城、隕霜，臣初信之，以臣心況，徒虛語耳！

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the sincerity of dog and horse cannot move others, just as human sincerity cannot move Heaven; collapsing walls and falling frost—I once believed these, but measured against my heart they are empty words!
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that the sincerity of dog and horse cannot move others, just as human sincerity cannot move Heaven; collapsing walls and falling frost—I once believed these, but measured against my heart they are empty words!

sentences.zh: 若葵藿之傾葉太陽，雖不為回光，然向之者誠也。

translations.literal: Like sunflower and bean tendril turning their leaves to the sun—though they do not make it turn back its light, yet their turning is sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Like sunflower and bean tendril turning their leaves to the sun—though they do not make it turn back its light, yet their turning is sincere.

sentences.zh: 竊自比葵藿，若降天地之施，垂三光之明者，實在陛下。

translations.literal: I compare myself in secret to sunflower and bean tendril; if there is one who bestows Heaven and Earth's grace and lets the three luminaries shine down, it is truly Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I compare myself in secret to sunflower and bean tendril; if there is one who bestows Heaven and Earth's grace and lets the three luminaries shine down, it is truly Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣聞《文子》曰：『不為福始，不為禍先。

translations.literal: I have heard in the Wenzi: "Do not be the first to bring fortune, do not be the first to bring calamity."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard in the Wenzi: "Do not be the first to bring fortune, do not be the first to bring calamity."

sentences.zh: 』今之否隔，友於同憂，而臣獨倡言者，實不願於聖世有不蒙施之物，欲陛下崇光被時雍之美，宣緝熙章明之德也！

translations.literal: " The present estrangement grieves brothers alike, yet I alone speak out—not because I wish anything in this sage age to go unblessed, but because I desire Your Majesty to exalt the radiance of an age of harmony and proclaim the bright, illustrious virtue of glorious peace!
translations.idiomatic: " The present estrangement grieves brothers alike, yet I alone speak out—not because I wish anything in this sage age to go unblessed, but because I desire Your Majesty to exalt the radiance of an age of harmony and proclaim the bright, illustrious virtue of glorious peace!

sentences.zh: 」詔報曰：「蓋教化所由，各有隆敝，非皆善始而惡終也，事使之然。

translations.literal: " An edict in reply said, "Teaching and transformation each have their rise and decline; not all begin well and end badly—circumstances make it so.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict in reply said, "Teaching and transformation each have their rise and decline; not all begin well and end badly—circumstances make it so.

sentences.zh: 今令諸國兄弟情禮簡怠，妃妾之家膏沐疏略，本無禁錮諸國通問之詔也。

translations.literal: Now I order that brotherly feeling and ritual among the feudal states have grown slack, and gifts of toilet goods to consorts' households sparse—there was never an edict forbidding the states to exchange visits.
translations.idiomatic: Brotherly feeling and ritual among the feudal states have grown slack, and gifts to consorts' households sparse—there was never an edict forbidding the states to exchange visits.

sentences.zh: 矯枉過正，下吏懼譴，以至於此耳。

translations.literal: Correcting the bent went too far; lower officials feared punishment, and matters came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Correcting the bent went too far; lower officials feared punishment, and matters came to this.

sentences.zh: 已敕有司，如王所訴。

translations.literal: I have already instructed the relevant offices according to what the prince pleaded.
translations.idiomatic: I have already instructed the relevant offices according to what the prince pleaded.

sentences.zh: 植復上疏曰：「昔漢文發代，疑朝有變，宋昌曰：『內有朱虛、東牟之親，外有齊、楚、淮南、琅邪，此則磐石之宗，願王勿疑。

translations.literal: Zhi again submitted a memorial saying, "Formerly when Emperor Wen of Han set out from Dai he suspected change in the court; Song Chang said, "Within are the kin of Zhuxu and Dongmou; without are Qi, Chu, Huainan, and Langye—these are the bedrock clans; I pray Your Highness do not doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi submitted another memorial: "When Emperor Wen of Han set out from Dai he suspected turmoil in the capital; Song Chang said, "Within are the kin of Zhuxu and Dongmou; without are Qi, Chu, Huainan, and Langye—these are bedrock clans; I pray Your Highness do not doubt."

sentences.zh: 』臣伏惟陛下遠覽姬文二虢之援，中慮周成召、畢之輔，下存宋昌磐石之固。

translations.literal: " I humbly consider that Your Majesty looks far to King Wen of Zhou's support from the two Guo states, reflects midmost on King Cheng of Zhou's assistance from the Duke of Shao and the Duke of Bi, and preserves below Song Chang's bedrock solidity.
translations.idiomatic: " I humbly consider that Your Majesty looks far to King Wen of Zhou's support from the two Guo states, reflects on King Cheng of Zhou's assistance from the Duke of Shao and the Duke of Bi, and preserves below Song Chang's bedrock solidity.

sentences.zh: 臣聞羊質虎皮，見草則悅，見豺則戰，忘其皮之虎也。

translations.literal: I have heard that a sheep in tiger's skin delights at the sight of grass but trembles at the sight of jackals, forgetting that its skin is tiger's.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a sheep in tiger's skin delights at the sight of grass but trembles at the sight of jackals, forgetting that its skin is tiger's.

sentences.zh: 今置將不良，有似於此。

translations.literal: Now if the generals appointed are unfit, it is somewhat like this.
translations.idiomatic: Now if the generals appointed are unfit, it is somewhat like this.

sentences.zh: 故語曰：『患為之者不知，知之者不得為也。

translations.literal: Hence the saying: "The one who suffers the trouble does not understand it; the one who understands it cannot act."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "The one who suffers the trouble does not understand it; the one who understands it cannot act."

sentences.zh: 』昔管、蔡放誅，周、召作弼；

translations.literal: " Formerly Guan and Cai were executed for rebellion, and the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao served as assistants;
translations.idiomatic: " Formerly Guan and Cai were executed for rebellion, and the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao served as assistants;

sentences.zh: 叔魚陷刑，叔向贊國。

translations.literal: Shuyu fell into punishment, yet Shuxiang aided the state.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyu fell into punishment, yet Shuxiang aided the state.

sentences.zh: 三監之釁，臣自當之；

translations.literal: The offense of the Three Overseers—I should bear it myself;
translations.idiomatic: The offense of the Three Overseers—I should bear it myself;

sentences.zh: 二南之輔，求必不遠。

translations.literal: assistants like those of the Two Souths—sought, they cannot be far.
translations.idiomatic: assistants like those of the Two Souths—sought, they cannot be far.

sentences.zh: 華宗貴族籓王之中，必有應斯舉者。

translations.literal: Among the splendid clans, noble houses, and feudal princes there must be one fit for this role.
translations.idiomatic: Among the splendid clans, noble houses, and feudal princes there must be one fit for this role.

sentences.zh: 夫能使天下傾耳注目者，當權者是也。

translations.literal: What makes the world incline its ears and fix its eyes is whoever holds power.
translations.idiomatic: What makes the world incline its ears and fix its eyes is whoever holds power.

sentences.zh: 故謀能移主，威能懾下。

translations.literal: Thus counsel can sway the ruler and authority can awe subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Thus counsel can sway the ruler and authority can awe subordinates.

sentences.zh: 豪右執政，不在親戚，權之所在，雖疏必重，勢之所去，雖親必輕。

translations.literal: When powerful magnates hold government, it is not among kin; where power lies, though distant one is weighty; where influence departs, though close one is slighted.
translations.idiomatic: When powerful magnates hold government, kinship counts for nothing; where power lies, even the distant grow weighty; where influence departs, even kin are slighted.

sentences.zh: 蓋取齊者田族，非呂宗也；

translations.literal: Those who seized Qi were the Tian clan, not the house of Lü;
translations.idiomatic: Those who seized Qi were the Tian clan, not the house of Lü;

sentences.zh: 分晉者趙、魏，非姬姓也。

translations.literal: those who divided Jin were Zhao and Wei, not surnamed Ji.
translations.idiomatic: those who divided Jin were Zhao and Wei, not of the house of Ji.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty examine this.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty examine this.

sentences.zh: 苟吉專其位，凶離其患者，異姓之臣也。

translations.literal: If fortune attends those who monopolize their posts and disaster those who leave them, these are ministers of another surname.
translations.idiomatic: If fortune attends those who monopolize their posts and disaster those who leave them, these are ministers of another surname.

sentences.zh: 欲國之安，祈家之貴，存共其榮，歿同其禍者，公族之臣也。

translations.literal: Those who desire the state's peace, pray for the clan's honor, share glory in life and share calamity in death—these are ministers of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Those who desire the state's peace, pray for the clan's honor, share glory in life and share calamity in death—these are ministers of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 今反公族疏而異姓親，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Now the imperial clan is kept distant while those of other surnames are drawn near—I am privately perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial clan is kept distant while those of other surnames are drawn near—I am privately perplexed.

sentences.zh: 今臣與陛下踐冰履炭，登山浮澗，寒溫燥濕，高下共之，豈得離陛下哉！

translations.literal: Now your servant and Your Majesty tread ice and walk on coals, climb mountains and ford streams, share cold and heat, dryness and damp, high and low—how could I leave Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Now your servant and Your Majesty tread ice and walk on coals, climb mountains and ford streams, share cold and heat, dryness and damp, high and low—how could I leave Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 不勝憤懣，拜表陳情。

translations.literal: Unable to bear my indignation, I bow and present this table stating my feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear my indignation, I bow and present this memorial stating my feelings.

sentences.zh: 若有不合，乞且藏之書府，不便滅棄，臣死之後，事或可思。

translations.literal: If anything does not accord, I beg that it be stored for now in the archive and not lightly destroyed; after my death the matter may yet be pondered.
translations.idiomatic: If anything does not accord, I beg that it be stored for now in the archive and not lightly destroyed; after my death the matter may yet be pondered.

sentences.zh: 若有毫釐少掛聖意者，乞出之朝堂，使夫博古之士，糾臣表之不合義者，如是則臣願足矣。

translations.literal: If the slightest thing offends the sage mind, I beg it be brought forth in court so that masters versed in antiquity may correct what in my memorial does not accord with right principle—then my wish would be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: If the slightest thing offends Your mind, I beg it be brought forth in court so that masters versed in antiquity may correct what in my memorial does not accord with right principle—then my wish would be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 」帝但以優文答報而已。

translations.literal: " The emperor only replied with soothing words and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor only replied with soothing words and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔曰：「先帝著令，不欲使諸王在京都者，謂幼主在位，母后攝政，防微以漸，關諸盛衰也。

translations.literal: Eighth month, an edict said, "The late emperor issued an order that he did not wish princes to remain in the capital because, when a young ruler holds the throne and the empress dowager regents, guarding against trouble from the small and gradual bears on rise and decline.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict said, "The late emperor issued an order that he did not wish princes to remain in the capital because, when a young ruler holds the throne and the empress dowager regents, guarding against trouble from the small and gradual bears on rise and decline.

sentences.zh: 朕惟不見諸王十有二載，悠悠之懷，能不興思！

translations.literal: I reflect that I have not seen the princes for twelve years—how can my distant longing fail to stir my thoughts!
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that I have not seen the princes for twelve years—how can my distant longing fail to stir my thoughts!

sentences.zh: 其令諸王及宗室公侯各將適子一人朝明年正月，後有少主、母后在宮者，自如先帝令。

translations.literal: Let the princes and the imperial clan's dukes and marquises each bring one legitimate son to court in the first month of next year; hereafter, when there is a young ruler and an empress dowager regent in the palace, follow the late emperor's order as before.
translations.idiomatic: Let the princes and the imperial clan's dukes and marquises each bring one legitimate son to court in the first month of next year; hereafter, when there is a young ruler and an empress dowager regent in the palace, follow the late emperor's order as before.

sentences.zh: 9漢丞相亮之攻祁山也，李平留後，主督運事。

translations.literal: 9. When Han Chancellor Liang attacked Qishan, Li Ping remained behind and was in charge of supervising transport.
translations.idiomatic: 9. When Zhuge Liang attacked Qishan, Li Ping remained behind and supervised transport.

sentences.zh: 會天霖雨，平恐運糧不繼，遣參軍孤忠、督軍成籓喻指，呼亮來還；

translations.literal: It happened that heaven sent torrential rain; Ping feared grain transport could not keep up and sent Staff Officer Gu Zhong and Transport Supervisor Cheng Fan with instructions summoning Liang to return;
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains set in; Ping feared supplies could not keep up and sent Staff Officer Gu Zhong and Transport Supervisor Cheng Fan with instructions summoning Liang to return;

sentences.zh: 亮承以退軍。

translations.literal: Liang accepted this and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Liang accepted this and withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 平聞軍退，乃更陽驚，說「軍糧饒足，何以便歸！

translations.literal: When Ping heard the army had withdrawn, he then openly feigned surprise, saying, "Army grain is abundant—why withdraw so soon!"
translations.idiomatic: When Ping heard the army had withdrawn, he then openly feigned surprise, saying, "Army grain is abundant—why withdraw so soon!"

sentences.zh: 」又欲殺督運岑述以解己不辦之責。

translations.literal: " He also wished to kill Transport Supervisor Cen Shu to absolve himself of failure in his duties.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wished to kill Transport Supervisor Cen Shu to absolve himself of failure in his duties.

sentences.zh: 又表漢主，說「軍偽退，欲以誘賊與戰。

translations.literal: He also memorialized the Han ruler, saying, "The army feigned retreat to lure the enemy into battle."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized the Han ruler, saying, "The army feigned retreat to lure the enemy into battle."

sentences.zh: 」亮具出其前後手筆書疏，本末違錯。

translations.literal: " Liang produced in full his earlier and later handwritten letters and memorials, which contradicted each other from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang produced in full his earlier and later handwritten letters and memorials, which contradicted each other from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 平辭窮情竭，首謝罪負。

translations.literal: Ping's words were exhausted and his feelings spent; he bowed his head and acknowledged guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's words were exhausted and his feelings spent; he bowed his head and acknowledged guilt.

sentences.zh: 於是亮表平前後過惡，免官，削爵土，徙梓潼郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liang memorialized Ping's offenses past and present; he was dismissed from office, stripped of rank and fief, and moved to Zitong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Liang memorialized Ping's offenses past and present; he was dismissed from office, stripped of rank and fief, and moved to Zitong commandery.

sentences.zh: 復以平子豐為中郎將、參軍事，出教敕之曰：「吾與君父子戮力以獎漢室，表都護典漢中，委君於東關，謂至心震動，終始可保，何圖中乖乎！

translations.literal: Liang again appointed Ping's son Feng as General of the Gentlemen of the Household and Staff Officer, issuing an instruction to him saying, "Your father and I joined forces to aid the Han house; I memorialized him as Area Commander-in-Chief governing Hanzhong and entrusted you at the eastern passes, thinking your utmost sincerity would hold from start to finish—who expected such a breach midway!"
translations.idiomatic: Liang again appointed Ping's son Feng as General of the Gentlemen of the Household and Staff Officer, issuing an instruction to him saying, "Your father and I joined forces to aid the Han house; I memorialized him as Area Commander-in-Chief governing Hanzhong and entrusted you at the eastern passes, thinking your utmost sincerity would hold from start to finish—who expected such a breach midway!"

sentences.zh: 若都護思負一意，君與公琰推心從事，否可復通，逝可復還也。

translations.literal: If the Area Commander-in-Chief reflects on his single-minded betrayal, you and Gongyan should deal with him in open sincerity—what is severed may be joined again, what has departed may return."
translations.idiomatic: If the Area Commander-in-Chief reflects on his betrayal, you and Fei Yi should deal with him in open sincerity—what is severed may be joined again, what has departed may return."

sentences.zh: 詳思斯戒，明吾用心！

translations.literal: Ponder this admonition carefully and understand my intent!"
translations.idiomatic: Ponder this admonition carefully and understand my intent!"

sentences.zh: 亮又與蔣琬、董允書曰：「孝起前為吾說正方腹中有鱗甲，鄉黨以為不可近。

translations.literal: Liang also wrote to Jiang Wan and Dong Yun: "Xiaoqi once told me that Zhengfang has scales in his belly and that neighbors consider him unapproachable.
translations.idiomatic: Liang also wrote to Jiang Wan and Dong Yun: "Xiaoqi once told me that Li Yan has scales in his belly and that neighbors consider him unapproachable.

sentences.zh: 吾以為鱗甲者但不當犯之耳，不圖復有蘇、張之事出於不意，可使孝起知之。

translations.literal: I thought 'scales' meant only that one should not provoke him—who expected Su and Zhang tactics to emerge unexpectedly? You may let Xiaoqi know."
translations.idiomatic: I thought 'scales' meant only that one should not provoke him—who expected Su and Zhang tactics to emerge unexpectedly? You may let Xiaoqi know."

sentences.zh: 」孝起者，衛尉南陽陳震也。

translations.literal: " Xiaoqi was Commandant of the Guards Chen Zhen of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaoqi was Commandant of the Guards Chen Zhen of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 10冬，十月，吳主使中郎將孫布詐降，以誘揚州刺史王淩，吳主伏兵於阜陵以俟之。

translations.literal: 10. Winter, tenth month, the Lord of Wu sent General of the Gentlemen of the Household Sun Bu to feign surrender and lure Yang Province Inspector Wang Ling; the Lord of Wu stationed ambush troops at Fuling to await him.
translations.idiomatic: 10. In winter, the tenth month, Sun Quan sent General of the Gentlemen of the Household Sun Bu to feign surrender and lure Yang Province Inspector Wang Ling; Sun Quan stationed ambush troops at Fuling to await him.

sentences.zh: 布遣人告淩云：「道遠不能自致，乞兵見迎。

translations.literal: Bu sent someone to tell Ling, "The road is long and I cannot come in person; I beg troops to meet and welcome me."
translations.idiomatic: Bu sent someone to tell Ling, "The road is long and I cannot come in person; I beg troops to meet and welcome me."

sentences.zh: 」淩騰布書，請兵馬迎之。

translations.literal: " Ling forwarded Bu's letter and requested troops and horses to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ling forwarded Bu's letter and requested troops and horses to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 征東將軍滿寵以為必詐，不與兵，而為淩作報書曰：「知識邪正，欲避禍就順，去暴歸道，甚相嘉尚。

translations.literal: Eastern Campaigning General Man Chong thought it must be a ruse and would not give troops, but wrote a reply for Ling saying, "Knowing right from wrong, wishing to flee calamity and follow what is fitting, leaving violence and returning to the Way—this is greatly to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Campaigning General Man Chong thought it must be a ruse and would not give troops, but wrote a reply for Ling saying, "Knowing right from wrong, wishing to flee calamity and follow what is fitting, leaving violence and returning to the Way—this is greatly to be praised.

sentences.zh: 今欲遣兵相迎，然計兵少則不足相衛，多則事必遠聞。

translations.literal: Now I wish to send troops to welcome you, yet if the force is small it will not suffice to protect you; if large, the affair will surely be heard far and wide.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to send troops to welcome you, yet if the force is small it will not suffice to protect you; if large, the affair will surely be heard far and wide.

sentences.zh: 且先密計以成本志，臨時節度其宜。

translations.literal: First make secret plans to accomplish your intent, then adjust measures as circumstances require."
translations.idiomatic: First make secret plans to accomplish your intent, then adjust measures as circumstances require."

sentences.zh: 」會寵被書入朝，敕留府長史，「若淩欲往迎，勿與兵也。

translations.literal: " It happened that Chong was summoned to court by imperial letter; he ordered the chief clerk left at headquarters, "If Ling wishes to go welcome him, do not give troops."
translations.idiomatic: " It happened that Chong was summoned to court by imperial letter; he ordered the chief clerk left at headquarters, "If Ling wishes to go welcome him, do not give troops."

sentences.zh: 」淩於後索兵不得，乃單遣一督將步騎七百人往迎之，布夜掩襲，督將迸走，死傷過半。

translations.literal: " Later Ling requested troops but could not obtain them; he then sent alone one supervising general with seven hundred infantry and cavalry to welcome Bu. Bu raided by night; the supervising general fled in disorder, and more than half were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Ling requested troops but could not obtain them; he then sent alone one supervising general with seven hundred infantry and cavalry to welcome Bu. Bu raided by night; the supervising general fled in disorder, and more than half were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 淩，允之兄子也。

translations.literal: Ling was the son of Yun's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was the son of Yun's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 先是淩表寵年過耽酒，不可居方任。

translations.literal: Earlier Ling had memorialized that Chong was advanced in years and addicted to wine, unfit to hold a regional post.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ling had memorialized that Chong was advanced in years and addicted to wine, unfit to hold a regional post.

sentences.zh: 帝將召寵，給事中郭謀曰：「寵為汝南太守、豫州刺史二十餘年，有勳方岳；

translations.literal: The emperor was about to summon Chong; Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Guo Mou said, "Chong served as Administrator of Runan and Inspector of Yuzhou for more than twenty years, with merit in the regions;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to summon Chong; Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Guo Mou said, "Chong served as Administrator of Runan and Inspector of Yuzhou for more than twenty years, with merit in the regions;

sentences.zh: 及鎮淮南，吳人憚之。

translations.literal: when he garrisoned Huainan, the Wu people feared him.
translations.idiomatic: when he garrisoned Huainan, the Wu people feared him.

sentences.zh: 若不如所表，將為所窺，可令還朝，問以東方事以察之。

translations.literal: If he is not as the memorial states, he will be spied upon; he may be ordered back to court and questioned on eastern affairs to observe him."
translations.idiomatic: If he is not as the memorial states, he will be spied upon; he may be ordered back to court and questioned on eastern affairs to observe him."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 既至，體氣康強，帝慰勞遣還。

translations.literal: When he arrived, his constitution was robust and healthy; the emperor comforted him and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, his constitution was robust and healthy; the emperor comforted him and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 11十一月，戊戌晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: 11. Eleventh month, last day of the cycle Wuxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 11. In the eleventh month, on the last day of the cycle Wuxu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 12十二月，戊午，博平敬侯華歆卒。

translations.literal: 12. Twelfth month, day Wuwu, Marquis Jing of Boping, Hua Xin, died.
translations.idiomatic: 12. In the twelfth month, on the day Wuwu, Hua Xin, Marquis Jing of Boping, died.

sentences.zh: 13丁卯，吳大赦，改明年元曰嘉禾。

translations.literal: 13. Day Dingmao, Wu proclaimed a general amnesty and changed next year's era name to Jiahe.
translations.idiomatic: 13. On the day Dingmao, Wu proclaimed a general amnesty and changed next year's era name to Jiahe.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，吳主少子建昌侯慮卒。

translations.literal: 1. Spring, first month, the Lord of Wu's youngest son, Marquis of Jianchang Lü, died.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, Sun Quan's youngest son, Marquis of Jianchang Lü, died.

sentences.zh: 太子登自武昌入省吳主，因自陳久離定省，子道有闕；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Deng came from Wuchang to visit the Lord of Wu and confessed that long absence from regular attendance had left a gap in filial duty;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Deng came from Wuchang to visit Sun Quan and confessed that long absence from regular attendance had left a gap in filial duty;

sentences.zh: 又陳陸遜忠勤，無所顧憂。

translations.literal: he also stated that Lu Xun was loyal and diligent, leaving nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: he also stated that Lu Xun was loyal and diligent, leaving nothing to worry about.

sentences.zh: 乃留建業。

translations.literal: He then remained at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: He then remained at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 2二月，詔改封諸侯王，皆以郡為國。

translations.literal: 2. Second month, an edict changed the enfeoffments of feudal princes so that each took a commandery as his state.
translations.idiomatic: 2. In the second month, an edict changed the enfeoffments of feudal princes so that each took a commandery as his state.

sentences.zh: 3帝愛女淑卒，帝痛之甚，追謚平原懿公主，立廟洛陽，葬於南陵。

translations.literal: 3. The emperor's beloved daughter Shu died; the emperor grieved deeply, posthumously titled her Princess Yi of Pingyuan, erected a temple in Luoyang, and buried her at Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: 3. The emperor's beloved daughter Shu died; the emperor grieved deeply, posthumously titled her Princess Yi of Pingyuan, erected a temple in Luoyang, and buried her at Nanling.

sentences.zh: 取甄后從孫黃與之合葬，追封黃為列侯，為之置後，襲爵。

translations.literal: He took Empress Zhen's collateral descendant Huang to be buried with her, posthumously enfeoffed Huang as a ranked marquis, established an heir for him, and had the title inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He took Empress Zhen's collateral descendant Huang to be buried with her, posthumously enfeoffed Huang as a ranked marquis, established an heir for him, and had the title inherited.

sentences.zh: 帝欲自臨送葬，又欲幸許。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to attend the funeral in person and also wished to visit Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to attend the funeral in person and also wished to visit Xu.

sentences.zh: 司空陳群諫曰：「八歲下殤，禮所不備，況未期月，而以成人禮送之，加為制服，舉朝素衣，朝夕哭臨，自古以來，未有此比。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chen Qun remonstrated: "Burial rites for a child who dies before eight are not provided for in ritual; moreover, not yet a full month old, yet you send her off with adult rites, add mourning garments, have the whole court in white, and mourn morning and evening—since antiquity there has been nothing like this.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chen Qun remonstrated: "Burial rites for a child who dies before eight are not provided for in ritual; moreover, not yet a full month old, yet you send her off with adult rites, add mourning garments, have the whole court in white, and mourn morning and evening—since antiquity there has been nothing like this.

sentences.zh: 而乃復自往視陵，親臨祖載！

translations.literal: Yet you would again go in person to view the tomb and attend the sending-off rites!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would again go in person to view the tomb and attend the sending-off rites!

sentences.zh: 願陛下抑割無益有損之事，此萬國之至望也。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty restrain what is useless and harmful—this is the utmost hope of the ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty restrain what is useless and harmful—this is the utmost hope of the realm.

sentences.zh: 又聞車駕欲幸許昌，二宮上下，皆悉俱東，舉朝大小，莫不驚怪。

translations.literal: I also hear the imperial carriage wishes to visit Xuchang, and both palaces above and below would all move east together—the whole court great and small is startled and amazed.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear the imperial carriage wishes to visit Xuchang, and both palaces above and below would all move east together—the whole court great and small is startled and amazed.

sentences.zh: 或言欲以避衰，或言欲以便移殿捨，或不知何故。

translations.literal: Some say you wish to avoid ill fortune, some say to facilitate moving palace quarters, some do not know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Some say you wish to avoid ill fortune, some say to facilitate moving palace quarters, some do not know the reason.

sentences.zh: 臣以為吉凶有命，禍福由人，移走求安，則亦無益。

translations.literal: I consider that fortune and misfortune have their mandate, calamity and blessing depend on people—moving about to seek safety is likewise of no use.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that fortune and misfortune have their mandate, calamity and blessing depend on people—moving about to seek safety is likewise of no use.

sentences.zh: 若必當移避，繕治金墉城西宮及孟津別宮，皆可權時分止，何為舉宮暴露野次！

translations.literal: If you must move to avoid harm, repairing the western palace at Jinyong and the separate palace at Mengjin could both serve as temporary halts—why expose the whole palace in the open countryside!
translations.idiomatic: If you must move to avoid harm, repairing the western palace at Jinyong and the separate palace at Mengjin could both serve as temporary halts—why expose the whole palace in the open countryside!

sentences.zh: 公私煩費，不可計量。

translations.literal: Public and private trouble and expense cannot be calculated.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private trouble and expense cannot be calculated.

sentences.zh: 且吉士賢人，猶不妄徙其家，以寧鄉邑，使無恐懼之心，況乃帝王萬國之主，行止動靜，豈可輕脫哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, even worthy gentlemen do not lightly move their households, so as to settle their villages and leave no heart of fear—how much more the emperor, lord of ten thousand states: his comings and goings, his movements and stillness—how can they be lightly cast aside!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, even worthy gentlemen do not lightly move their households, so as to settle their villages and leave no heart of fear—how much more the emperor, lord of ten thousand states: his comings and goings, his movements and stillness—how can they be lightly cast aside!

sentences.zh: 」少府楊阜曰：「文皇帝、武宣皇后崩，陛下皆不送葬，所以重社稷，備不虞也；

translations.literal: " Minister Steward Yang Fu said, "When Emperor Wen and Empress Wuxuan died, Your Majesty did not attend the burials, thereby honoring the altars of soil and grain and guarding against the unforeseen;
translations.idiomatic: " Minister Steward Yang Fu said, "When Emperor Wen and Empress Wuxuan died, Your Majesty did not attend the burials, thereby honoring the altars of soil and grain and guarding against the unforeseen;

sentences.zh: 何至孩抱之赤子而送葬也哉！

translations.literal: how could you go so far as to send off a suckling infant in burial!"
translations.idiomatic: how could you go so far as to send off a suckling infant in burial!"

sentences.zh: 」帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not listen to any of this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen to any of this.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸酉，行東巡。

translations.literal: Third month, day Guiyou, he made an eastern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day Guiyou, he made an eastern tour.

sentences.zh: 4吳主遣將軍周賀、校尉裴潛乘海之遼東，從公孫淵求馬。

translations.literal: 4. The Lord of Wu sent General Zhou He and Commandant Pei Qian by sea to Liaodong to request horses from Gongsun Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: 4. Sun Quan sent General Zhou He and Commandant Pei Qian by sea to Liaodong to request horses from Gongsun Yuan.

sentences.zh: 初，虞翻性疏直，數有酒失，又好抵忤人，多見謗毀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu Fan's nature was blunt and upright; he often erred through drink and also liked to offend people, and was much slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yu Fan's nature was blunt and upright; he often erred through drink and also liked to offend people, and was much slandered.

sentences.zh: 吳主嘗與張昭論及神仙，翻指昭曰：「彼皆死人而語神仙，世豈有仙人也！

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu once discussed immortals with Zhang Zhao; Fan pointed at Zhao and said, "Those are dead men speaking of immortals—are there immortals in the world!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan once discussed immortals with Zhang Zhao; Fan pointed at Zhao and said, "Those are dead men speaking of immortals—are there immortals in the world!"

sentences.zh: 」吳主積怒非一，遂徙翻交州。

translations.literal: " The Lord of Wu's accumulated anger was not slight; he then moved Fan to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan's accumulated anger was not slight; he then moved Fan to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 及周賀等之遼東，翻聞之，以為五溪宜討，遼東絕遠，聽使來屬，尚不足取，今去人財以求馬，既非國利，又恐無獲。

translations.literal: When Zhou He and others went to Liaodong, Fan heard of it and thought the Five Streams should be attacked; Liaodong is utterly remote—even if they came to submit it would hardly be worth taking; now to send men and wealth for horses is neither national profit nor, I fear, likely to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou He and others went to Liaodong, Fan heard of it and thought the Five Streams should be attacked; Liaodong is utterly remote—even if they came to submit it would hardly be worth taking; now to send men and wealth for horses is neither national profit nor, I fear, likely to succeed.

sentences.zh: 欲諫不敢，作表以示呂岱，岱不報。

translations.literal: He wished to remonstrate but dared not; he drafted a memorial and showed it to Lü Dai, who did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to remonstrate but dared not; he drafted a memorial and showed it to Lü Dai, who did not reply.

sentences.zh: 為愛憎所白，復徙蒼梧猛陵。

translations.literal: Reported by those who loved or hated him, he was again moved to Mengling in Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Reported by those who loved or hated him, he was again moved to Mengling in Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 5夏，四月，壬寅，帝如許昌。

translations.literal: 5. Summer, fourth month, day Renyin, the emperor went to Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: 5. In summer, the fourth month, on the day Renyin, the emperor went to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 1五月，皇子殷卒。

translations.literal: 1. Fifth month, the imperial son Yin died.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In the fifth month, the prince Yin died.

sentences.zh: 7秋，七月，以衛尉董昭為司徒。

translations.literal: 7. Autumn, seventh month, Commandant of the Guards Dong Zhao was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In autumn, the seventh month, Commandant of the Guards Dong Zhao was made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 8九月，帝行如摩陂，治許昌宮，起景福、承光殿。

translations.literal: 8. Ninth month, the emperor went to Mobei, repaired the palace at Xuchang, and erected the Jingfu and Chengguang halls.
translations.idiomatic: 8. In the ninth month, the emperor went to Mobei, repaired the palace at Xuchang, and erected the Jingfu and Chengguang halls.

sentences.zh: 9公孫淵陰懷貳心，數與吳通。

translations.literal: 9. Gongsun Yuan secretly harbored disloyal intent and repeatedly communicated with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: 9. Gongsun Yuan secretly harbored disloyal intent and repeatedly communicated with Wu.

sentences.zh: 帝使汝南太守田豫督青州諸軍自海道，幽州刺史王雄自陸道討之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Administrator of Runan Tian Yu to supervise Qing Province armies by the sea route and Inspector of You Wang Xiong by the land route to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Administrator of Runan Tian Yu to supervise Qing Province armies by the sea route and Inspector of You Wang Xiong by the land route to attack him.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍蔣濟諫曰：「凡非相吞之國，不侵叛之臣，不宜輕伐。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant Jiang Ji remonstrated: "Generally, states that are not devouring each other and subjects who do not invade or rebel should not be lightly attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant Jiang Ji remonstrated: "Generally, states that are not devouring each other and subjects who do not invade or rebel should not be lightly attacked.

sentences.zh: 伐之而不能制，是驅使為賊也。

translations.literal: To attack and fail to control them is to drive them to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: To attack and fail to control them is to drive them to become bandits.

sentences.zh: 故曰：『虎狼當路，不治狐狸。

translations.literal: Hence the saying: "When tigers and wolves block the road, do not bother with foxes."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "When tigers and wolves block the road, do not bother with foxes."

sentences.zh: 』先除大害，小害自己。

translations.literal: " Remove the great harm first, and lesser harms will resolve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: " Remove the great harm first, and lesser harms will resolve themselves.

sentences.zh: 今海表之地，累世委質，歲選計、孝，不乏職貢，議者先之。

translations.literal: Now the lands beyond the sea have for generations submitted allegiance, yearly selecting candidates for the provincial and filial-piety examinations, never failing in tribute—those who discuss policy put them first.
translations.idiomatic: Now the lands beyond the sea have for generations submitted allegiance, yearly selecting candidates for the provincial and filial-piety examinations, never failing in tribute—those who discuss policy put them first.

sentences.zh: 正使一舉便克，得其民不足益國，得其財不足為富；

translations.literal: Even if one stroke conquered them, gaining their people would not enrich the state, gaining their wealth would not make it rich;
translations.idiomatic: Even if one stroke conquered them, gaining their people would not enrich the state, gaining their wealth would not make it rich;

sentences.zh: 倘不如意，是為結怨失信也。

translations.literal: if things do not go as wished, this is to forge enmity and break faith."
translations.idiomatic: if things do not go as wished, this is to forge enmity and break faith."

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 豫等往，皆無功，詔令罷軍。

translations.literal: Yu and the others went but all achieved nothing; an edict ordered the armies withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and the others went but all achieved nothing; an edict ordered the armies withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 豫以吳使周賀等垂還，歲晚風急，必畏漂浪，東道無岸，當赴成山，成山無藏船之處，遂輒以兵屯據成山。

translations.literal: Yu thought the Wu envoys Zhou He and others were about to return; late in the year winds are fierce and they would surely fear being driven by waves—the eastern route has no harbors and they would head for Chengshan; Chengshan has no place to hide ships, so he promptly stationed troops to hold Chengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu thought the Wu envoys Zhou He and others were about to return; late in the year winds are fierce and they would surely fear being driven by waves—the eastern route has no harbors and they would head for Chengshan; Chengshan has no place to hide ships, so he promptly stationed troops to hold Chengshan.

sentences.zh: 賀等還至成山，遇風，豫勒兵擊賀等，斬之。

translations.literal: He and the others returned to Chengshan, met wind, and Yu led troops to attack He and the others and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He and the others returned to Chengshan, met wind, and Yu led troops to attack He and the others and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 吳主聞之，始思虞翻之言，乃召翻於交州。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu heard of this and first reflected on Yu Fan's words; he then summoned Fan from Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan heard of this and first reflected on Yu Fan's words; he then summoned Fan from Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 會翻已卒，以其喪還。

translations.literal: It happened that Fan had already died; his coffin was brought back.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Fan had already died; his coffin was brought back.

sentences.zh: 10十一月，庚寅，陳思王植卒。

translations.literal: 10. Eleventh month, day Gengyin, Prince of Chen Si, Zhi, died.
translations.idiomatic: 10. In the eleventh month, on the day Gengyin, Cao Zhi, Prince of Chen Si, died.

sentences.zh: 11十二月，帝還許昌宮。

translations.literal: 11. Twelfth month, the emperor returned to the palace at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: 11. In the twelfth month, the emperor returned to the palace at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 12侍中劉曄為帝所親重。

translations.literal: 12. Palace Attendant Liu Ye was personally favored and esteemed by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: 12. Palace Attendant Liu Ye was personally favored and esteemed by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝將伐蜀，朝臣內外皆曰不可。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to attack Shu; court officials within and without all said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to attack Shu; court officials within and without all said it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 曄入與帝議，則曰可伐；

translations.literal: When Ye entered to discuss with the emperor, he said it could be attacked;
translations.idiomatic: When Ye entered to discuss with the emperor, he said it could be attacked;

sentences.zh: 出與朝臣言，則曰不可。

translations.literal: when he went out and spoke to court officials, he said it could not.
translations.idiomatic: when he went out and spoke to court officials, he said it could not.

sentences.zh: 曄有膽智，言之皆有形。

translations.literal: Ye had courage and wisdom; what he said always took concrete form.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had courage and wisdom; what he said always took concrete form.

sentences.zh: 中領軍楊暨，帝之親臣，又重曄，執不可伐之議最堅，每從內出，輒過曄，曄講不可之意。

translations.literal: Central Army Commander Yang Ji was the emperor's intimate minister and also esteemed Ye; he held most firmly to the view that attack was impossible, and whenever he came out from within he would pass by Ye, and Ye would explain why it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Commander Yang Ji was the emperor's intimate minister and also esteemed Ye; he held most firmly to the view that attack was impossible, and whenever he came out from within he would pass by Ye, and Ye would explain why it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 後暨與帝論伐蜀事，暨切諫，帝曰：「卿書生，焉知兵事！

translations.literal: Later Ji discussed attacking Shu with the emperor; Ji remonstrated urgently. The emperor said, "You are a bookish man—how would you know military affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: Later Ji discussed attacking Shu with the emperor; Ji remonstrated urgently. The emperor said, "You are a bookish man—how would you know military affairs!"

sentences.zh: 」暨謝曰：「臣言誠不足采，侍中劉曄，先帝謀臣，常曰蜀不可伐。

translations.literal: " Ji apologized: "My words truly are not worth adopting; Palace Attendant Liu Ye, the late emperor's strategist, always said Shu could not be attacked."
translations.idiomatic: " Ji apologized: "My words truly are not worth adopting; Palace Attendant Liu Ye, the late emperor's strategist, always said Shu could not be attacked."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「曄與吾言蜀可伐。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Ye told me Shu could be attacked."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Ye told me Shu could be attacked."

sentences.zh: 」暨曰：「曄可召質也。

translations.literal: " Ji said, "Ye may be summoned to verify this."
translations.idiomatic: " Ji said, "Ye may be summoned to verify this."

sentences.zh: 」詔召曄至，帝問曄，終不言。

translations.literal: " An edict summoned Ye; when the emperor questioned Ye, he said nothing in the end.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict summoned Ye; when the emperor questioned Ye, he said nothing in the end.

sentences.zh: 後獨見，曄責帝曰：「伐國，大謀也，臣得與聞大謀，常恐瞇夢漏洩以益臣罪，焉敢向人言之！

translations.literal: Later, seeing him alone, Ye reproached the emperor: "Attacking a state is a great plan; having been allowed to hear a great plan, I constantly fear dozing or dreaming and leaking it to increase my guilt—how dare I speak of it to others!"
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing him alone, Ye reproached the emperor: "Attacking a state is a great plan; having been allowed to hear a great plan, I constantly fear dozing or dreaming and leaking it to increase my guilt—how dare I speak of it to others!"

sentences.zh: 夫兵詭道也，軍事未發，不厭其密。

translations.literal: Warfare is the way of deception; before military affairs are launched, one cannot have too much secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: Warfare is the way of deception; before military affairs are launched, one cannot have too much secrecy.

sentences.zh: 陛下顯然露之，臣恐敵國已聞之矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has openly exposed it—I fear the enemy state has already heard.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has openly exposed it—I fear the enemy state has already heard.

sentences.zh: 」於是帝謝之。

translations.literal: " At this the emperor apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then apologized to him.

sentences.zh: 曄見出，責暨曰：「夫釣者中大魚，則縱而隨之，須可制而後牽，則無不得也。

translations.literal: When Ye came out, he reproached Ji, saying: "When an angler hooks a big fish, he lets it run and follows it; only when he can control it does he pull—in this way nothing escapes him.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Ye left the audience, he rebuked Yang Ji: "When a fisherman hooks a large fish, he lets it run and follows it; only when he can control it does he haul it in—and then nothing gets away.

sentences.zh: 人主之威，豈徒大魚而已！

translations.literal: The sovereign's authority—is it only a big fish!
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's authority is no mere fish on the line!

sentences.zh: 子誠直臣，然計不足采，不可不精思也。

translations.literal: You are indeed a straight minister, yet your plan was not worth adopting; you must not fail to think carefully."
translations.idiomatic: You are a loyal, forthright minister—but your scheme was not worth taking. You must think these matters through more carefully."

sentences.zh: 」暨亦謝之。

translations.literal: " Ji also apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji apologized as well.

sentences.zh: 或謂帝曰：「曄不盡忠，善伺上意所趨而合之。

translations.literal: Someone told the emperor: "Ye is not fully loyal; he is good at watching where the ruler's inclination tends and aligning with it.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the emperor, "Liu Ye is not wholly loyal. He is adept at reading where Your Majesty's mind is tending and shaping his answers to match it.

sentences.zh: 陛下試與曄言，皆反意而問之，若皆與所問反者，是曄常與聖意合也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty might try speaking with Ye, asking everything contrary to his own intent; if in every case he answers opposite to what was asked, that shows Ye constantly matches the sacred intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty might test him by speaking with Liu Ye and asking the opposite of what you mean. If he always answers contrary to the question, that proves he habitually aligns with the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 每問皆同者，曄之情必無所復逃矣。

translations.literal: If every question gets the same answer, Ye's true feelings will have nowhere left to hide."
translations.idiomatic: But if every question draws the same answer, Liu Ye's true disposition will have nowhere left to hide."

sentences.zh: 」帝如言以驗之，果得其情，從此疏焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor tested him as described, and indeed got at his true disposition; from then on he kept Ye at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tested him as advised, uncovered his true character, and from that time kept him at arm's length.

sentences.zh: 曄遂發狂，出為大鴻臚，以憂死。

translations.literal: Ye thereupon went mad, was sent out as Grand Herald of the Hong, and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye soon went mad, was transferred out as Grand Herald of the Hong, and died of distress.

sentences.zh: ::《傅子》曰：巧詐不如拙誠，信矣！

translations.literal: Fu Zi says: "Clever deceit cannot match clumsy sincerity—truly so!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zi says: "Clever deceit cannot match plain sincerity—how true!"

sentences.zh: 以曄之明智權計，若居之以德義，行之以忠信，古之上賢，何以加諸！

translations.literal: With Ye's intelligence and resourceful scheming, if he had been situated in virtue and righteousness and conducted himself in loyalty and trustworthiness, how could the great sages of antiquity have surpassed him!
translations.idiomatic: Given Liu Ye's intelligence and shrewd calculation, had he grounded himself in virtue and righteousness and acted in loyalty and good faith, what could the greatest sages of old have added to him!

sentences.zh: 獨任才智，不敦誠愨，內失君心，外困於俗，卒以自危，豈不惜哉！

translations.literal: Relying solely on wit and ability, not fostering sincere integrity, he lost the ruler's heart within and was trapped by convention without, and in the end brought peril on himself—is this not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: He relied on talent alone and did not cultivate sincere integrity. Within he lost the ruler's trust; without he was hemmed in by public opinion—and in the end endangered himself. Is that not a pity!

sentences.zh: 13曄嘗譖尚書令陳矯專權，矯懼，以告其子騫。

translations.literal: 13. Ye once slandered Director of the Masters of Writing Chen Qiao for monopolizing power; Qiao was afraid and told his son Qian.
translations.idiomatic: 13. Liu Ye once accused Director of the Masters of Writing Chen Qiao of monopolizing power. Qiao was alarmed and told his son Qian.

sentences.zh: 騫曰：「主上明聖，大人大臣，今若不合，不過不作公耳。

translations.literal: Qian said: "The lord is enlightened and sagely, a great man among ministers; if you are not in accord now, at worst you simply will not be made a duke."
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "The sovereign is enlightened and sagacious, and you are a great minister. If you are out of favor for the moment, at worst you will simply not be enfeoffed as a duke."

sentences.zh: 」後數日，帝意果解。

translations.literal: " Several days later, the emperor's mind indeed eased.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, the emperor's suspicions did indeed lift.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎樂安廉昭以才能得幸，昭好抉擿群臣細過以求媚於上。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing Attendant Lian Zhao of Le'an won favor through talent; Zhao liked to pick out petty faults of the various ministers to curry favor above.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Writing Attendant Lian Zhao of Le'an had won favor through ability. Zhao liked to ferret out petty faults among the ministers to ingratiate himself with the throne.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎杜恕上疏曰：「伏見廉昭奏左丞曹璠以罰當關不依詔，坐判問。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Du Shu submitted a memorial saying: "I have seen that Lian Zhao impeached Left Assistant Director Cao Fan for punishment at the barrier gate not according to the edict, and he sits in judgment and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Du Shu submitted a memorial, saying, "I have observed that Lian Zhao impeached Left Assistant Director Cao Fan because punishment at the barrier gate was not carried out according to the edict, and he sits in judgment over the matter.

sentences.zh: 又云：『諸當坐者別奏。

translations.literal: He also said: 'All who should be punished are to be reported separately.'
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, 'All who merit punishment are to be reported separately.'

sentences.zh: 』尚書令陳矯自奏不敢辭罰，亦不敢陳理，志意懇惻。

translations.literal: Director Chen Qiao submitted on his own behalf that he dared not decline punishment, yet dared not state his case; his intent was earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Director Chen Qiao submitted on his own account that he dared not refuse punishment, yet dared not plead his case—his intent earnest and sincere.

sentences.zh: 臣竊愍然為朝廷惜之！

translations.literal: I secretly grieve for the court on this account!
translations.idiomatic: I cannot help grieving for the court over this!

sentences.zh: 古之帝王所以能輔世長民者，莫不遠得百姓之歡心，近盡群臣之智力。

translations.literal: The reason the emperors and kings of antiquity could aid the age and nurture the people was that none failed to win the common people's hearts from afar and to exhaust the ministers' intelligence near at hand.
translations.idiomatic: The reason emperors and kings of old could sustain the age and nurture the people was that none failed to win the people's hearts from afar and to draw fully on their ministers' intelligence close at hand.

sentences.zh: 今陛下憂勞萬機，或親燈火，而庶事不康，刑禁日弛。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty toils over the myriad affairs of state, sometimes personally tending the lamps, yet the multitude of tasks is not well ordered and punishments and prohibitions grow lax day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Today Your Majesty labors over ten thousand matters of state, sometimes even tending the lamps yourself, yet public affairs are not well ordered and law and discipline grow slack by the day.

sentences.zh: 原其所由，非獨臣不盡忠，亦主不能使也。

translations.literal: Tracing the cause, it is not only that ministers do not exhaust loyalty—it is also that the ruler cannot employ them.
translations.idiomatic: The root cause lies not only in ministers failing to give their full loyalty, but also in the ruler's inability to make use of them.

sentences.zh: 百里奚愚於虞而智於秦，豫讓苟容中行而著節智伯，斯則古人之明驗矣。

translations.literal: Baili Xi was foolish in Yu yet wise in Qin; Yu Rang endured humiliation under Zhonghang yet showed integrity toward Zhi Bo—this is the clear proof of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Baili Xi seemed dull in Yu yet proved wise in Qin; Yu Rang bore humiliation under Zhonghang yet showed his integrity toward Zhi Bo—the ancients left clear proof of this.

sentences.zh: 若陛下以為今世無良才，朝廷乏賢佐，豈可追望稷、契之遐蹤，坐待來世之俊乂乎！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty thinks that in the present age there are no good talents and the court lacks worthy assistants, how can you look back to the distant footsteps of Hou Ji and Qi, and sit waiting for outstanding men of a future age!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty believes that our age has no true talent and the court lacks worthy helpers, can you really look back to the distant footsteps of Hou Ji and Qi, and sit idle waiting for heroes of some future generation!

sentences.zh: 今之所謂賢者，盡有大官而享厚祿矣，然而奉上之節未立，向公之心不一者，委任之責不專，而俗多忌諱故也。

translations.literal: Those now called worthy all hold high office and enjoy thick salaries, yet the duty of serving above is not established and the heart turned toward the public is not unified—because the responsibility of appointment is not exclusive, and because custom has many taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Those now called worthy all hold high rank and draw heavy salaries—yet the discipline of serving the throne is not established, and hearts are not single-mindedly turned toward the public good, because delegated responsibility is not exclusive and because custom is thick with taboos.

sentences.zh: 臣以為忠臣不必親，親臣不必忠。

translations.literal: I hold that loyal ministers need not be intimate, and intimate ministers need not be loyal.
translations.idiomatic: I believe loyal ministers need not be favorites, and favorite ministers need not be loyal.

sentences.zh: 今有疏者毀人而陛下疑其私報所憎，譽人而陛下疑其私愛所親，左右或因之以進憎愛之說，遂使疏者不敢毀譽，以至政事損益，亦皆有嫌。

translations.literal: Now when memorial writers criticize others Your Majesty suspects private revenge against those they hate; when they praise others Your Majesty suspects private affection for those they favor—and attendants at the side may use this to advance talk of hatred and love, so that memorial writers dare not criticize or praise, until even gains and losses in government affairs all come under suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Today, when a memorial writer denounces someone, Your Majesty suspects private vengeance against an enemy; when one praises someone, Your Majesty suspects private favor toward a friend. Attendants at your side may then use this to feed talk of hatred and affection, until critics and praisers alike fall silent—and even the benefit or harm of policy comes under suspicion.

sentences.zh: 陛下當思所以闡廣朝臣之心，篤厲有道之節，使之自同古人，垂名竹帛，反使如廉昭者擾亂其間，臣懼大臣將遂容身保位，坐觀得失，為來世戒也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to consider how to broaden the hearts of court ministers and earnestly encourage the integrity of those who follow the Way, so that they may of themselves match the ancients and leave their names on bamboo and silk—yet instead you let men like Lian Zhao stir turmoil among them. I fear great ministers will then simply preserve themselves and their posts, sitting by to watch gains and losses, and this will become a warning to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should consider how to open the hearts of the court and earnestly foster the integrity of those who follow the Way, so that they may match the ancients of their own accord and leave their names in the histories—yet instead you allow men like Lian Zhao to sow disorder among them. I fear that senior ministers will then merely secure their persons and their posts, sitting by to watch what succeeds and what fails, and that this will stand as a warning to ages yet to come.

sentences.zh: 昔周公戒魯侯曰：『無使大臣怨乎不以。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Duke of Zhou admonished the Lord of Lu, saying: 'Do not let great ministers resent that they are not employed.'
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Duke of Zhou warned the Lord of Lu, saying, "Do not let great ministers resent that they are not put to use."

sentences.zh: 』言不賢則不可為大臣，為大臣則不可不用也。

translations.literal: The meaning is: if they are not worthy they cannot serve as great ministers; if they serve as great ministers they cannot go unused.
translations.idiomatic: The point is this: if a man is unworthy he should not be made a great minister; if he is made a great minister he must not be left unused.

sentences.zh: 《書》數舜之功，稱去四凶，不言有罪無問大小則去也。

translations.literal: The Documents recount Shun's achievements and praise the removal of the Four Evils—it does not say that when there is guilt, regardless of great or small, they are removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents recount Shun's achievements and praise the banishment of the Four Evils—it does not say that whenever there is guilt, great or small alike, the guilty are removed.

sentences.zh: 今者朝臣不自以為不能，以陛下為不任也；

translations.literal: At present court ministers do not think themselves incapable—they think Your Majesty does not employ them;
translations.idiomatic: Today the court ministers do not think themselves incapable—they think Your Majesty will not employ them;

sentences.zh: 不自以為不知，以陛下為不問也。

translations.literal: they do not think themselves ignorant—they think Your Majesty does not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: they do not think themselves ignorant—they think Your Majesty does not ask.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不遵周公之所以用，大舜之所以去，使侍中、尚書坐則侍帷幄，行則從華輦，親對詔問，各陳所有，則群臣之行皆可得而知，患能者進，闇劣者退，誰敢依違而不自盡。

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not follow how the Duke of Zhou employed men and how great Shun removed the unfit—so that Palace Attendants and Directors of the Masters of Writing, when seated, attend within the curtains, and when walking, follow the splendid carriage; face the edicts and questions in person, each stating what he has—then the conduct of all ministers can be known, the able advanced and the dim and inferior retired, and who would dare hang back and not give his utmost?
translations.idiomatic: Why does Your Majesty not follow how the Duke of Zhou employed men and how great Shun removed the unfit—so that Palace Attendants and Directors of the Masters of Writing, when seated, attend within the curtains, and when you travel, follow the imperial carriage; face your questions in person, each stating what he knows—then the conduct of every minister can be known, the able advanced and the incompetent dismissed, and who would dare hang back and not give his utmost?
