sentences.zh: 以陛下之聖明，親與群臣論議政事，使群臣人得自盡，賢愚能否，在陛下之所用。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's sagely brilliance, personally debating government affairs with the ministers and letting each man give his utmost, whether worthy or foolish, able or not—all lies in whom Your Majesty employs.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's sagely brilliance, debating policy with the ministers in person and letting each give his utmost—whether a man is worthy or foolish, able or not, all depends on whom Your Majesty puts to use.

sentences.zh: 以此治事，何事不辦；

translations.literal: Governing affairs in this way, what matter would not be settled;
translations.idiomatic: Governing in this way, what affair would not be settled;

sentences.zh: 以此建功，何功不成！

translations.literal: achieving merit in this way, what merit would not be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: achieving merit in this way, what achievement would not be won!

sentences.zh: 每有軍事，詔書常曰：『誰當憂此者邪？

translations.literal: Whenever there is military business, edicts often say: 'Who should worry over this?'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there is military business, edicts often say, "Who should worry over this?"

sentences.zh: 吾當自憂耳。

translations.literal: I myself shall worry over it.'
translations.idiomatic: "I myself shall worry over it."

sentences.zh: 』近詔又曰：『憂公忘私者必不然，但先公後私即自辦也。

translations.literal: A recent edict also said: 'Those who worry for the public and forget the private surely do not exist; only put the public first and the private after, and you will manage it yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: A recent edict also said, "Those who forget self for the sake of the public surely do not exist; only put the public first and the private after, and you will manage it yourself."

sentences.zh: 』伏讀明詔，乃知聖思究盡下情，然亦怪陛下不治其本而憂其末也。

translations.literal: " Having read these enlightened edicts in prostration, I know the sacred thought exhaustively reaches to the feelings below—yet I also marvel that Your Majesty does not govern the root but worries over the branches.
translations.idiomatic: Reading these enlightened edicts with reverence, I know Your Majesty's mind reaches down to the feelings of those below—yet I also wonder that Your Majesty does not treat the root of the matter but troubles over the branches.

sentences.zh: 人之能否，實有本性，雖臣亦以為朝臣不盡稱職也。

translations.literal: Whether men are able or not truly lies in their nature; even I think court ministers do not all fill their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Whether men are capable truly lies in their nature; even I think the court ministers do not all fill their posts.

sentences.zh: 明主之用人也，使能者不能遺其力，而不能者不得處非其任。

translations.literal: When an enlightened ruler employs men, he makes the able unable to withhold their strength, and the unable unable to occupy posts not their own.
translations.idiomatic: When an enlightened ruler employs men, he makes the able unable to withhold their strength, and the unable unable to hold posts beyond their capacity.

sentences.zh: 選舉非其人，未必為有罪也；

translations.literal: To select and recommend someone unfit is not necessarily a crime;
translations.idiomatic: To recommend someone unfit is not necessarily a crime;

sentences.zh: 舉朝共容非其人，乃為怪耳。

translations.literal: for the whole court together to tolerate someone unfit—that is what is strange.
translations.idiomatic: for the whole court together to tolerate someone unfit—that is what is truly strange.

sentences.zh: 陛下知其不盡力也而代之憂其職，知其不能也而教之治其事，豈徒主勞而臣逸哉，雖聖賢並世，終不能以此為治也！

translations.literal: Your Majesty knows they do not exert their strength yet worries over their duties for them; knows they are unable yet teaches them to govern their affairs—is this merely the ruler toiling while ministers rest? Even if sage and worthy lived together in one age, in the end governance could not be achieved in this way!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty knows they do not exert themselves yet worries over their duties in their stead; knows they are incapable yet instructs them in how to govern their affairs—is this merely the ruler laboring while ministers take their ease? Even if sage and worthy lived in the same age, in the end the realm could not be governed this way!

sentences.zh: 陛下又患臺閣禁令之不密，人事請屬之不絕，作迎客出入之制，以惡吏守寺門，斯實未得為禁之本也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty also worries that the prohibitions of the terrace pavilions are not strict, that requests and patronage in personnel matters never cease, and has made regulations for receiving guests coming in and out, with wicked clerks guarding temple gates—this truly has not yet grasped the root of prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty also worries that the terrace offices' prohibitions are not strict, that requests and patronage in appointments never cease, and has instituted rules for guests entering and leaving, with corrupt clerks guarding the gates—this truly has not yet struck at the root of the problem.

sentences.zh: 昔漢安帝時，少府竇嘉辟廷尉郭躬無罪之兄子，猶見舉奏，章劾紛紛；

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor An of Han, Junior Steward Dou Jia recruited the nephew of Commandant of Justice Guo Gong, who was without guilt, yet still was impeached, memorials of accusation flying;
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor An of Han, Junior Steward Dou Jia recruited the nephew of Commandant of Justice Guo Gong, though he was guiltless, yet still was impeached, memorials of accusation flying thick;

sentences.zh: 近司隸校尉孔羨辟大將軍狂悖之弟，而有司嘿爾，望風希指，甚於受屬。

translations.literal: recently Director of Retainers Kong Xian recruited the younger brother of the Grand General who was violent and rebellious, yet the responsible officials were silent, looking to the wind and hoping to hit the mark—worse than receiving patronage.
translations.idiomatic: recently Director of Retainers Kong Xian recruited the younger brother of the Grand General, who was violent and rebellious, yet the responsible officials were silent, watching the wind and hoping to hit the mark—worse than taking patronage outright.

sentences.zh: 選舉不以實者也。

translations.literal: This is selection and recommendation not according to fact.
translations.idiomatic: This is recommendation not grounded in fact.

sentences.zh: 嘉有親戚之寵，躬非社稷重臣，猶尚如此；

translations.literal: Jia had the favor of kinship, Gong was not a great minister of state, and still it was so;
translations.idiomatic: Jia had the favor of kinship; Gong was not a pillar minister of state—and still it was so;

sentences.zh: 以今況古，陛下自不督必行之罰以絕阿黨之原耳。

translations.literal: judging the present by antiquity, Your Majesty yourself has not supervised punishments that must be carried out to cut off the source of faction.
translations.idiomatic: judging the present by antiquity, Your Majesty yourself has not enforced punishments that must be carried out, to cut off the source of cliques.

sentences.zh: 出入之制，與惡吏守門，非治世之具也。

translations.literal: Regulations for going in and out, and wicked clerks guarding gates, are not the tools of a well-governed age.
translations.idiomatic: Rules for comings and goings, and corrupt clerks at the gates, are not the instruments of a well-governed age.

sentences.zh: 使臣之言少蒙察納，何患於奸不削滅，而養若廉昭等乎！

translations.literal: If my words receive even a little examination and acceptance, what worry is there that treachery will not be cut down, or that you would nurture men like Lian Zhao!
translations.idiomatic: If my words receive even a little of Your Majesty's scrutiny and acceptance, what worry is there that treachery will not be cut down—or that you would continue to nurture men like Lian Zhao!

sentences.zh: 夫糾擿奸宄，忠事也；

translations.literal: To expose and impeach treachery and villainy is a loyal act;
translations.idiomatic: To expose and impeach treachery and villainy is a loyal act;

sentences.zh: 然而世憎小人行之者，以其不顧道理而苟求容進也。

translations.literal: yet the age hates petty men who do it, because they disregard principle and recklessly seek favor and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: yet the age hates petty men who do it, because they disregard principle and recklessly seek favor and advancement.

sentences.zh: 若陛下不復考其終始，必以違眾迕世為奉公，密行白人為盡節，焉有通人大才而更不能為此邪？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty no longer examines their beginning and end, and must take opposing the multitude and going against the age as serving the public, and secretly reporting on people as exhausting loyalty—are there men of broad talent and great ability who yet could not do this?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty no longer examines how such conduct begins and ends, and must take opposing the multitude and going against the world as serving the public, and secret denunciation as exhausting loyalty—are there men of broad talent and great ability who could not do this?

sentences.zh: 誠顧道理而弗為耳。

translations.literal: They truly consider principle and do not do it.
translations.idiomatic: They simply heed principle—and refuse.

sentences.zh: 使天下皆背道而趨利，則人主之所最病者也，陛下將何樂焉！

translations.literal: To make all under Heaven turn their backs on the Way and rush toward profit is what the ruler most dreads—what pleasure will Your Majesty find in it!
translations.idiomatic: To make all under Heaven turn their backs on the Way and rush toward profit is what a ruler dreads most—what pleasure can Your Majesty take in that!

sentences.zh: 」恕，畿之子也。

translations.literal: " Shu was the son of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shu was the son of Du Ji.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗卒至尚書門，陳矯跪問帝曰：「陛下欲何之？

translations.literal: The emperor once suddenly arrived at the gate of the Masters of Writing; Chen Qiao knelt and asked the emperor: "Your Majesty, where are you going?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once arrived unannounced at the gate of the Masters of Writing. Chen Qiao knelt and asked, "Your Majesty, where are you going?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「欲案行文書耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I merely wish to examine the documents in transit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I only wish to look over the documents in transit."

sentences.zh: 」矯曰：「此自臣職分，非陛下所宜臨也。

translations.literal: " Qiao said: "This is my own duty as a minister; it is not what Your Majesty should personally attend to."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao said, "That is my duty as a minister—not something Your Majesty should attend to in person."

sentences.zh: 若臣不稱其職，則請就黜退，陛下宜還。

translations.literal: If I do not fill my post, then I ask to be dismissed and removed; Your Majesty should return."
translations.idiomatic: If I am not equal to my post, then dismiss me—but Your Majesty should go back."

sentences.zh: 」帝慚，回車而反。

translations.literal: " The emperor was ashamed, turned his carriage and went back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was ashamed, turned his carriage, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問矯：「司馬公忠貞，可謂社稷之臣乎？

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Qiao: "The Lord Marshal is loyal and steadfast—can he be called a pillar of state?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Qiao, "The Lord Marshal is loyal and steadfast—can he be called a pillar of state?"

sentences.zh: 」矯曰：「朝廷之望也，社稷則未知也。

translations.literal: " Qiao said: "He is the court's hope; as to being a pillar of state, that remains to be seen."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao said, "He is the court's hope; whether he is a pillar of state remains to be seen."

sentences.zh: 14吳陸遜引兵向廬江，論者以為宜速救之。

translations.literal: 14. Wu's Lu Xun led troops toward Lujiang; debaters thought relief should be sent swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: 14. In Wu, Lu Xun led troops toward Lujiang; opinion held that relief should be sent swiftly.

sentences.zh: 滿寵曰：「廬江雖小，將勁兵精，守則經過。

translations.literal: Man Chong said: "Though Lujiang is small, its generals are strong and its troops elite; if defended, the enemy will pass by.
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong said, "Lujiang is small, but its commanders are strong and its troops elite. If it is held, the enemy will pass by.

sentences.zh: 又，賊捨船二百里來，後尾空絕，不來尚欲誘致，今宜聽其遂進。

translations.literal: Moreover, the rebels left their boats two hundred li behind; their rear trail is empty and cut off—even if they do not come, we still wish to lure them; now it is fitting to let them advance as they will.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the enemy abandoned their boats two hundred li away; their rear is empty and cut off. Even if they did not come, we would still wish to lure them in. Now we should let them advance as they will.

sentences.zh: 但恐走不可及耳。

translations.literal: I only fear they may flee beyond our reach."
translations.idiomatic: I only fear they may flee before we can catch them."

sentences.zh: 」乃整軍趨楊宜口，吳人聞之，夜遁。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he arrayed the army and hastened to Yangyikou; when the Wu men heard of it, they fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon arrayed his army and hastened to Yangyikou. When the Wu forces heard of it, they fled by night.

sentences.zh: 是時，吳人歲有來計。

translations.literal: At this time the Wu men every year had plans to come.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Wu forces every year planned raids.

sentences.zh: 滿寵上疏曰：「合肥城南臨江湖，北遠壽春，賊攻圍之，得據水為勢；

translations.literal: Man Chong submitted a memorial saying: "Hefei south adjoins rivers and lakes; north it is far from Shouchun. When rebels attack and besiege it, they can take advantage of water for momentum;
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong submitted a memorial, saying, "Hefei lies south against rivers and lakes, and north is far from Shouchun. When rebels attack and besiege it, they can use the water to their advantage;

sentences.zh: 官兵救之，當先破賊大輩，然後圍乃得解。

translations.literal: when government troops go to relieve it, they must first break the enemy's main force, and only then can the siege be lifted.
translations.idiomatic: when government troops go to relieve it, they must first break the enemy's main force before the siege can be lifted.

sentences.zh: 賊往甚易，而兵往救之甚難，宜移城內之兵，其西三十里，有奇險可依，更立城以固守，此為引賊平地而掎其歸路，於計為便。

translations.literal: The rebels go easily, yet troops going to relieve go with great difficulty. It is fitting to move the troops within the city thirty li to the west, where there is marvelous terrain to rely on, and establish a new city to hold fast—this draws the rebels onto level ground and seizes their route of return; for planning it is advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy can advance easily, yet relief troops advance with great difficulty. The troops within the city should be moved thirty li west, where there is excellent terrain to rely on, and a new city built to hold fast—this lures the enemy onto level ground and cuts their line of retreat. For strategy it is the better course.

sentences.zh: 」護軍將軍蔣濟議以為：「既示天下以弱，且望賊煙火而壞城，此為未攻而自拔；

translations.literal: " Protector-General Jiang Ji argued that "having already shown weakness to all under Heaven, and expecting the rebels' signal fires while abandoning the city—this is pulling out before being attacked;
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General Jiang Ji argued that "this would already show weakness to all under Heaven, and we would be watching the enemy's signal fires while tearing down our own walls—this is abandoning a city before it is even attacked;

sentences.zh: 一至於此，劫略無限，必淮北為守。

translations.literal: once it comes to this, plunder will be without limit, and we will surely be reduced to defending north of the Huai."
translations.idiomatic: once matters reach that point, plunder will know no limit, and we will surely be reduced to defending only north of the Huai."

sentences.zh: 」帝未許。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not approve.

sentences.zh: 寵重表曰：「孫子言：『兵者，詭道也，故能而示之不能，驕之以利，示之以懾，』此為形實不必相應也。

translations.literal: Chong submitted another memorial saying: "Master Sun said: 'Warfare is the way of deception; therefore able, yet show unable; entice with profit, display with awe'—this means form and reality need not correspond.
translations.idiomatic: Chong submitted another memorial, saying, "Master Sun said, 'Warfare is the way of deception; therefore be able yet show unable; entice with profit, display with awe'—meaning appearance and reality need not match.

sentences.zh: 又曰：『善動敵者形之。

translations.literal: He also said: 'One who skillfully moves the enemy gives him form.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said, 'One who skillfully moves the enemy gives him form.'

sentences.zh: 』今賊未至而移城卻內，所謂形而誘之也。

translations.literal: " Now the rebels have not arrived yet we move the city and withdraw inward—this is what is called giving form to entice them.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy has not arrived, yet we move the city and withdraw inward—this is precisely what is called giving form to lure them.

sentences.zh: 引賊遠水，擇利而動，舉得於外，而福生於內矣！

translations.literal: Draw the rebels away from the water, choose advantage and act, gain everything outside, and blessing is born within!
translations.idiomatic: Draw the enemy away from the water, choose the moment of advantage and strike, win everything abroad, and blessing will arise at home!"

sentences.zh: 」尚書趙咨以寵策為長，詔遂報聽。

translations.literal: " Director of the Masters of Writing Zhao Zi judged Chong's plan superior; an edict thereupon approved and permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Zhao Zi judged Chong's plan superior, and an edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，甲申，青龍見摩陂井中，二月，〔丁酉〕<ref>〔丁酉〕據《魏志．明帝紀》補。

translations.literal: 1. Spring, first month, on Jiashen day, an azure dragon appeared in the well at Mobei. Second month, [Dingyou]<ref>[Dingyou] supplied according to the Annals of Mingdi in the Records of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, during the first month, on the day Jiashen, an azure dragon was seen in the well at Mobei. In the second month, on the day Dingyou<ref>Supplied according to the Annals of Mingdi in the Records of Wei.

sentences.zh: </ref>，帝如摩陂觀龍，改元。

translations.literal: </ref>, the emperor went to Mobei to view the dragon and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: [End editorial note.] The emperor went to Mobei to see the dragon and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 2公孫淵遣校尉宿舒、郎中令孫綜奉表稱臣於吳；

translations.literal: 2. Gongsun Yuan sent Commandant Su Shu and Master of Ceremonies Sun Zong to submit a memorial declaring himself subject to Wu;
translations.idiomatic: 2. Gongsun Yuan sent Commandant Su Shu and Master of Ceremonies Sun Zong to submit a memorial declaring himself a subject of Wu;

sentences.zh: 吳主大悅，為之大赦。

translations.literal: the King of Wu was greatly pleased and proclaimed a general amnesty on his account.
translations.idiomatic: the King of Wu was greatly pleased and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 三月，吳主遣太常張彌、執金吾許晏、將軍賀達將兵萬人，金寶珍貨，九錫備物，乘海授淵，封淵為燕王。

translations.literal: Third month, the King of Wu sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhang Mi, Bearer of the Mace Xu Yan, and General He Da to lead ten thousand troops with gold, treasures, precious goods, and the full regalia of the Nine Bestowals, crossing the sea to invest Yuan, enfeoffing Yuan as King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the King of Wu sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhang Mi, Bearer of the Mace Xu Yan, and General He Da to lead ten thousand men with gold, treasures, precious goods, and the full regalia of the Nine Bestowals across the sea to invest Yuan as King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 舉朝大臣自顧雍以下皆諫，以為：「淵未可信而寵待太厚，但可遣吏兵護送舒、綜而已。

translations.literal: Ministers of the court from Gu Yong down all remonstrated, saying: "Yuan cannot yet be trusted and favor is too great; it is enough to send officials and troops to escort Shu and Zong back."
translations.idiomatic: The court ministers from Gu Yong down all remonstrated, saying, "Yuan cannot yet be trusted, and the favor shown him is too great. It is enough to send officials and troops to escort Shu and Zong home."

sentences.zh: 」吳主不聽。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 張昭曰：「淵背魏懼討，遠來求援，非本志也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao said: "Yuan turned his back on Wei in fear of punishment and came from afar seeking aid—this was not his original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao said, "Yuan turned against Wei in fear of punishment and came from afar seeking aid—this was not his original intent.

sentences.zh: 若淵改圖，欲自明於魏，兩使不反，不亦取笑於天下乎！

translations.literal: If Yuan changes his plan and wishes to make himself clear to Wei, and both envoys do not return, will we not become a laughingstock to all under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: If Yuan changes his plan and wishes to show his loyalty to Wei, and both envoys fail to return, will we not become a laughingstock to all under Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」吳主反覆難昭，昭意彌切。

translations.literal: The King of Wu argued back and forth with Zhao; Zhao's intent grew all the more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu argued back and forth with Zhao; Zhao's remonstrance grew all the more urgent.

sentences.zh: 吳主不能堪，案刀而怒曰：「吳國士人入宮則拜孤，出宮則拜君，孤之敬君亦為至矣，而數於眾中折孤，孤常恐失計！

translations.literal: The King of Wu could not bear it; he grasped his knife and said in anger: "Wu gentlemen enter the palace and bow to me, leave the palace and bow to you—my respect for you has also reached the utmost, yet you repeatedly humiliate me before the multitude. I constantly fear I may lose my temper!"
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu could not endure it. He seized his knife and said angrily, "Wu gentlemen enter the palace and bow to me, leave the palace and bow to you—my respect for you has reached the utmost, yet you repeatedly shame me before the multitude. I constantly fear I may lose my temper!"

sentences.zh: 」昭熟視吳主曰：「臣雖知言不用，每竭愚忠者，誠以太后臨崩，呼老臣於床下，遺詔顧命之言故在耳。

translations.literal: Zhao stared fixedly at the King of Wu and said: "Though I know my words are not heeded, each time I exhaust my foolish loyalty—it is truly because when the empress dowager was on her deathbed she called this old minister to her bedside, and the testamentary charge remains in my ears."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao fixed his gaze on the King of Wu and said, "Though I know my words go unheeded, each time I exhaust my foolish loyalty—it is because when the empress dowager lay dying she called this old minister to her bedside, and her testamentary charge still rings in my ears."

sentences.zh: 」因涕泣橫流。

translations.literal: " Thereupon tears streamed across his face.
translations.idiomatic: Tears then streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 吳主擲刀於地，與之對泣。

translations.literal: The King of Wu cast his knife to the ground and wept facing him.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu cast his knife aside and wept with him face to face.

sentences.zh: 然卒遣彌、晏往。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he still sent Mi and Yan forth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he still sent Zhang Mi and Xu Yan on their mission.

sentences.zh: 昭忿言之不用，稱疾不朝。

translations.literal: Zhao, resentful that his words were not used, claimed illness and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao, furious that his advice went unheeded, claimed illness and stopped attending court.

sentences.zh: 吳主恨之，土塞其門，昭又於內以土封之。

translations.literal: The King of Wu hated this and blocked his gate with earth; Zhao moreover sealed himself from within with earth.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu, in resentment, had earth piled against his gate; Zhang Zhao in turn walled himself in with earth from inside.

sentences.zh: 3夏，五月，戊寅，北海王蕤卒。

translations.literal: 3. Summer, fifth month, day Wuyin—the Prince of Beihai Rui died.
translations.idiomatic: 3. In summer, the fifth month, on day Wuyin, Prince Rui of Beihai died.

sentences.zh: 4閏月，庚寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: 4. Intercalary month, first day Gengyin—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 4. In the intercalary month, on the first day Gengyin of the cycle, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 5六月，洛陽宮鞠室災。

translations.literal: 5. Sixth month—the cuju court at the Luoyang palace suffered fire.
translations.idiomatic: 5. In the sixth month, the ball-court chamber in the Luoyang palace burned.

sentences.zh: 6鮮卑軻比能誘保塞鮮卑步度根與深結和親，自勒萬騎迎其累重於陘北。

translations.literal: 6. The Xianbei Kebineng enticed the frontier-guarding Xianbei Budugen into a deep pact of kinship by marriage, himself leading ten thousand horsemen to welcome Budugen's families and baggage north of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: 6. The Xianbei chieftain Kebineng drew the frontier-guarding Xianbei Budugen into a close marriage alliance and personally led ten thousand horsemen north of the Xing Pass to receive Budugen's kin and baggage train.

translations.literal: </ref>, to threaten Kebineng from without and pacify Budugen within.
translations.idiomatic: [End editorial note.] He would threaten Kebineng from without and keep Budugen in check within.

sentences.zh: 帝省表曰：「步度根已為比能所誘，有自疑心。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial and said: "Budugen has already been enticed by Kebineng and entertains suspicions on his own account.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor reviewed the memorial and said, "Budugen has already been won over by Kebineng and is liable to turn suspicious on his own.

sentences.zh: 今軌出軍，慎勿越塞過句注也。

translations.literal: Now that Gui marches out, take care not to cross the frontier passes beyond Juzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Bi Gui takes the field, take care not to cross the frontier passes beyond Juzhu.

sentences.zh: 」比詔書到，軌已進軍屯陰館，遣將軍蘇尚、董弼追鮮卑。

translations.literal: " When this edict arrived, Gui had already advanced and encamped at Yinguan, sending Generals Su Shang and Dong Bi in pursuit of the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the edict arrived, Bi Gui had already advanced and encamped at Yinguan, dispatching Generals Su Shang and Dong Bi to pursue the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 軻比能遣子將千餘騎迎步度根部落，與尚、弼相遇，戰於樓煩，二將沒，步度根與洩歸泥部落皆叛出塞，與軻比能合寇邊。

translations.literal: Kebineng sent his son with more than a thousand horsemen to welcome Budugen's tribe; they met Shang and Bi in battle at Loufan; both generals perished; Budugen and the tribes of Xiégūní all rebelled beyond the passes and joined Kebineng in raiding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Kebineng sent his son with over a thousand riders to welcome Budugen's people; they met Shang and Bi at Loufan and both Wei generals were killed; Budugen and Xiégūní's tribes fled beyond the passes and joined Kebineng in border raids.

sentences.zh: 帝遣驍騎將軍秦朗將中軍討之，軻比能乃走幕北，洩歸泥將其部眾來降。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Valiant Cavalry General Qin Lang to lead the central armies against them; Kebineng then fled north of the felt camps; Xiégūní led his tribesmen to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Valiant Cavalry General Qin Lang at the head of the central army to suppress them; Kebineng fled north beyond the tents, and Xiégūní brought his people in to surrender.

sentences.zh: 步度根尋為軻比能所殺。

translations.literal: Budugen was shortly thereafter killed by Kebineng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Budugen was killed by Kebineng.

sentences.zh: 7公孫淵知吳遠難恃，乃斬張彌、許晏等首，傳送京師，悉沒其兵資珍寶。

translations.literal: 7. Gongsun Yuan, knowing Wu was distant and hard to rely on, thereupon beheaded Zhang Mi, Xu Yan, and the rest, sent their heads to the capital, and confiscated all their troops' supplies and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: 7. Gongsun Yuan, seeing that Wu was far away and unreliable, beheaded Zhang Mi, Xu Yan, and their party, sent the heads to the Wei capital, and seized all their troops, supplies, and treasure.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，詔拜淵大司馬，封樂浪公。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month—an edict appointed Yuan Grand Marshal and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, an edict made Yuan Grand Marshal and enfeoffed him Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 吳主聞之，大怒曰：「朕年六十，世事難易，靡所不嘗。

translations.literal: The King of Wu heard and said in great anger: "I am sixty years old; easy and hard in worldly affairs—there is nothing I have not tasted.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Wu heard this he flew into a rage and said, "I am sixty years old; of hardship and ease in this world there is nothing I have not known.

sentences.zh: 近為鼠子所前卻，令人氣踴如山。

translations.literal: Recently to be pushed back by a ratling makes one's rage surge like a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To be turned back lately by a wretched mouse of a foe makes my fury surge like a mountain.

sentences.zh: 不自截鼠子頭以擲於海，無顏復臨萬國。

translations.literal: If I do not myself cut off that ratling's head and cast it into the sea, I have no face to face all nations again.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not cut off that rat's head myself and cast it into the sea, I have no face to rule the realm again.

sentences.zh: 就令顛沛，不以為恨！

translations.literal: Even if I should be overthrown, I would not count it a regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Even if I am ruined, I will not regret it!"

sentences.zh: 陸遜上疏曰：「陛下以神武之姿，誕膺期運，破操烏林，敗備西陵，禽羽荊州。

translations.literal: Lu Xun submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty, with a divinely martial bearing, received the mandate of the age, broke Cao at Wulin, defeated Liu at Xiling, and captured Guan in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty, with divine martial prowess, received Heaven's mandate, broke Cao Cao at Wulin, defeated Liu Bei at Xiling, and captured Guan Yu in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 斯三虜者，當世雄傑，皆摧其鋒。

translations.literal: These three foes were the heroes of the age, yet all had their edge broken.
translations.idiomatic: These three foes were the greatest men of the age, yet Your Majesty broke every one of them.

sentences.zh: 聖化所綏，萬里草偃，方蕩平華夏，總一大猷。

translations.literal: Where sacred transformation extends, grass bends for ten thousand li; you are about to sweep the Central Plains and gather the great design into one.
translations.idiomatic: Where your sacred rule reaches, the land bows for ten thousand li; you are on the verge of pacifying the Central Plains and uniting the realm under one design.

sentences.zh: 今不忍小忿而發雷霆之怒，違垂堂之戒，輕萬乘之重，此臣之所惑也。

translations.literal: Now, unwilling to bear a small resentment, you unleash thunderclap wrath, violate the warning of not standing beneath a falling beam, and lightly risk the weight of the imperial chariot—this is what your servant finds perplexing.
translations.idiomatic: Now, unwilling to endure a slight affront, you unleash thunderous wrath, ignore the admonition not to stand where a beam might fall, and lightly risk the weight of the imperial chariot—this is what perplexes your servant.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之，行萬里者不中道而輟足，圖四海者不懷細以害大。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that one who travels ten thousand li does not halt mid-journey, and one who plots the four seas does not let small matters harm the great.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that one who travels ten thousand li does not stop halfway, and one who plots to master the four seas does not let small grievances spoil the great design.

sentences.zh: 強寇在境，荒服未庭，陛下乘桴遠征，必致闚𨵦，戚至而憂，悔之無及。

translations.literal: With strong foes on the borders and distant lands not yet at court, if Your Majesty sails afar on campaign, you will surely invite prying eyes; when trouble arrives you will grieve—and regret will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: With powerful enemies on the frontier and distant lands not yet paying court, if Your Majesty sails on a distant campaign you will invite opportunists; when calamity strikes you will grieve—and regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 若使大事時捷，則淵不討自服。

translations.literal: If great affairs succeed in their season, Yuan will submit without being punished.
translations.idiomatic: If the great enterprise advances in its season, Yuan will submit without your needing to punish him.

sentences.zh: 今乃遠惜遼東眾之與馬，奈何獨欲捐江東萬安之本業而不惜乎！

translations.literal: Now you begrudge the men and horses of distant Liaodong—how can you alone be willing to cast away the foundation of ten thousand peace in Jiangdong and not regret it!"
translations.idiomatic: Now you begrudge Liaodong's distant men and horses—how can you be willing to throw away Jiangdong's foundation of lasting peace and feel no regret!"

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射薛綜上疏曰：「昔漢元帝欲御樓船，薛廣德請刎頸以血染車。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xue Zong submitted a memorial saying: "In former times Emperor Yuan of Han wished to board a tower ship; Xue Guangde asked to cut his throat and dye the carriage with blood.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xue Zong submitted a memorial saying, "Formerly Emperor Yuan of Han wished to board a tower ship; Xue Guangde offered to cut his throat and dye the carriage with his blood.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 水火之險至危，非帝王所宜涉也。

translations.literal: The peril of water and fire is utmost danger—not what an emperor should venture into.
translations.idiomatic: Water and fire are utmost peril—not what an emperor should brave.

sentences.zh: 今遼東戎貊小國，無城隍之固，備御之術，器械銖鈍，犬羊無政，往必禽克，誠如明詔。

translations.literal: Liaodong today is a petty Rong-Di state, without stout walls or arts of defense; its weapons are blunt as a few grains of copper; its people are dogs and sheep without governance—if you go, capture is certain, as your bright edict says.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong is a petty barbarian state without stout walls or proper defenses; its arms are crude, its people unruly sheep and dogs—as Your Majesty's edict says, conquest would be easy.

sentences.zh: 然其方土寒埆，穀稼不殖，民習鞍馬，轉徙無常，卒聞大軍之至，自度不敵，鳥驚獸駭，長驅奔竄，一人匹馬，不可得見，雖獲空地，守之無益，此不可一也。

translations.literal: Yet its soil is cold and barren, grain does not grow, the people are skilled with saddle and horse and wander without fixed abode; when they suddenly hear the great army arrive, judging themselves no match, they will scatter like startled birds and beasts, fleeing at a long gallop—one man, one horse, none to be seen; though you gain empty land, to hold it is no gain—this is the first reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the land is cold and barren, grain will not grow, and the people live on horseback, wandering without fixed abode; at news of a great army they will scatter like startled beasts—no man or horse to be found; though you seize empty territory, holding it profits nothing—first, the campaign cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 加又洪流滉漾，有成山之難，海行無常，風波難免，倏忽之間，人船異勢，雖有堯、舜之德，智無所施，賁、育之勇，力不得設，此不可二也。

translations.literal: Moreover the floods spread wide, with the peril of Chengsheng Mountain; sea travel has no constancy, winds and waves hard to avoid—in an instant men and ships part fates; though one had the virtue of Yao and Shun, wisdom could not be applied; though one had the courage of Ben and Yu, strength could not be deployed—this is the second reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the seas run vast and treacherous, with dangers like Chengsheng Mountain; voyages have no fixed course and storms are unavoidable—in an instant ship and crew may part fates; even Yao and Shun's virtue could not avail, even Ben and Yu's courage could not be used—second, the campaign cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 加以郁霧冥其上，鹼水蒸其下，善生流腫，轉相洿染，凡行海者，稀無斯患，此不可三也。

translations.literal: Added to this, dense fog lies above and brackish water steams below; sores and swellings thrive and infection spreads from one to another; of all who travel the sea, few escape this affliction—this is the third reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Add dense fog overhead and brackish vapors below, breeding sores that spread from man to man—few who sail the sea escape such sickness—third, the campaign cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 天生神聖，當乘時平亂，康此民物。

translations.literal: Heaven born the sacred—he should seize the time to pacify disorder and bring peace to this people.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven born the sacred ruler—he should seize the hour to pacify disorder and comfort the people.

sentences.zh: 今逆虜將滅，海內垂定，乃違必然之圖，尋至危之阻，忽九州之固，肆一朝之忿，既非社稷之重計，又開闢以來所未嘗有，斯誠群僚所以傾身側息，食不甘味，寢不安席者也。

translations.literal: Now the rebellious foe is about to perish and the realm within the seas is nearly settled; yet you turn from the inevitable design and seek the utmost peril, neglect the security of the nine provinces, and indulge a morning's wrath—this is neither the weighty plan of the altars of soil and grain nor anything attempted since the founding of the state; truly this is why the ministers lean their bodies and hold their breath, eat without tasting, and sleep without a mat.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rebel is nearly destroyed and the realm almost settled—yet you abandon the sure design for utmost peril, neglect the security of the nine provinces, and indulge a morning's wrath; this is no plan for the altars of state, nor anything tried since the realm was founded—no wonder your ministers hold their breath, eat without savor, and sleep without rest.

sentences.zh: 選曹尚書陸瑁上疏曰：「北寇與國，壤地連接，苟有間隙，應機而至。

translations.literal: Director of Selection Lu Kai submitted a memorial saying: "The northern foe and our state share contiguous territory; if a gap appears, they will come at the first opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Selection Lu Kai submitted a memorial saying, "The northern enemy borders our land; if a gap opens they will strike at the first chance.

sentences.zh: 夫所以為越海求馬，曲意於淵者，為赴目前之急，除腹心之疾也。

translations.literal: The reason for crossing the sea to seek horses and bending intent toward Yuan is to meet the urgent need before us and remove the malady at the heart.
translations.idiomatic: We cross the sea and court Yuan only to meet today's urgent need and remove the disease at our heart.

sentences.zh: 而更棄本追末，捐近治遠，忿以改規，激以動眾，斯乃猾虜所願聞，非大吳之至計也。

translations.literal: Yet now you abandon the root and chase the branch, cast off what is near to govern what is far, change plans in anger and stir the masses with wrath—this is what cunning foes wish to hear, not the supreme plan of Great Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now you abandon the root for the branch, neglect what is near to govern what is far, change course in anger and rouse the host—this is what cunning foes hope to hear, not Great Wu's supreme strategy.

sentences.zh: 又兵家之術，以功役相疲，勞逸相待，得失之間，所覺輒多。

translations.literal: Moreover in the art of war one wears down the enemy through labor and duty, matching fatigue against ease; in the interval between gain and loss one perceives much.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover war wears foes down through toil while matching fatigue against ease; in the balance of gain and loss much becomes clear.

sentences.zh: 且沓渚去淵，道裡尚遠，今到其岸，兵勢三分，使強者進取，次當守船，又次運糧，行人雖多，難得悉用。

translations.literal: Moreover Tazhu is still far from Yuan; when you reach the shore the army must divide into three parts—the strong advance, the next guard the ships, the last transport grain; though many march, it is hard to use them all.
translations.idiomatic: Tazhu is still far from Yuan; once ashore the army must split three ways—strongest to attack, next to guard the ships, last to haul grain; though many march, few can be fully employed.

sentences.zh: 加以單步負糧，經遠深入，賊地多馬，邀截無常。

translations.literal: Added to this, men carrying grain on foot, marching deep over long distances—in enemy land there are many horses and ambushes without warning.
translations.idiomatic: Men must carry grain on foot deep into enemy country where horses abound and ambushes strike without warning.

sentences.zh: 若淵狙詐，與北未絕，動眾之日，脣齒相濟；

translations.literal: If Yuan is cunning and not yet cut off from the north, the day you move the host lip and teeth will aid each other;
translations.idiomatic: If Yuan is cunning and still tied to the north, the day you mobilize they will aid each other like lip and teeth;

sentences.zh: 若實孑然無所憑賴，其畏怖遠迸，或難卒滅使天誅稽於朔野，山虜承間而起，恐非萬安之長慮也！

translations.literal: if he stands utterly without support, in fear he will flee far off, or be hard to destroy at once—making Heaven's punishment linger on the northern wastes while mountain barbarians rise in the interval—I fear this is not a plan for lasting peace!"
translations.idiomatic: if he stands utterly alone he may flee in terror and prove hard to destroy at once—Heaven's punishment lingering on the northern wastes while mountain tribes rise in the breach—I fear that is no plan for lasting peace!"

sentences.zh: 」吳主未許。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu would not agree.

sentences.zh: 瑁重上疏曰：「夫兵革者，固前代所以誅暴亂、威四夷也。

translations.literal: Kai again submitted a memorial saying: "Arms and armor are what former ages used to punish violence and awe the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai submitted again, saying, "Arms and armor are what former ages used to punish violence and awe the four barbarians.

sentences.zh: 然其役皆在奸雄已除，天下無事，從容廟堂之上，以餘議議之耳。

translations.literal: Yet their deployment is when treacherous heroes have been removed and all under Heaven is without affairs—at ease in the ancestral hall, with surplus counsel to spare.
translations.idiomatic: But they are deployed only after traitors are gone and the realm is at peace—when one deliberates at leisure in the ancestral hall.

sentences.zh: 至於中夏鼎沸，九域盤互之時，率須深根固本，愛力惜費，未有正於此時捨近治遠，以疲軍旅者也。

translations.literal: When the central lands seethe and the nine domains intertwine in conflict, one must take deep root and firm foundation, cherish strength and spare expense—never has anyone in such a time cast off what is near to govern what is far and weary the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the heartland boils and the nine domains clash, one must deepen roots and spare strength—never in such a time has a ruler cast off the near to govern the far and exhaust his armies.

sentences.zh: 昔尉佗叛逆，僭號稱帝，於時天下乂安，百姓康阜，然漢文猶以遠征不易，告喻而已。

translations.literal: Formerly when Zhao Tuo rebelled and arrogated the title of emperor, all under Heaven was then at peace and the people prosperous—yet Emperor Wen still held distant campaigns hard and contented himself with admonition.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Tuo rebelled and styled himself emperor, the realm was at peace and the people prosperous—yet Emperor Wen still deemed distant campaigns arduous and contented himself with admonition.

sentences.zh: 今凶桀未殄，疆場猶警，未宜以淵為先。

translations.literal: Now fierce villains are not yet destroyed and the borders still alert—Yuan should not be made the first priority.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce foes are not yet destroyed and the borders still alarmed—Yuan should not come first.

sentences.zh: 願陛下抑威任計，暫寧六師，潛神嘿規，以為後圖，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty restrain your might and trust to planning, for a time quiet the six armies, conceal your spirit in silent design, and take thought for what follows—the realm would be greatly fortunate!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to curb your wrath and trust to strategy, for a time rest the six armies, lay plans in silence, and look to what follows—the realm would be greatly fortunate!"

sentences.zh: 」吳主乃止。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu then desisted.

sentences.zh: 吳主數遣人慰謝張昭，昭因不起。

translations.literal: The King of Wu repeatedly sent men to comfort and apologize to Zhang Zhao; Zhao therefore did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu repeatedly sent envoys to comfort and apologize to Zhang Zhao; Zhao still would not attend court.

sentences.zh: 吳主因出，過其門呼昭，昭辭疾篤。

translations.literal: The King of Wu went out in person, passed his gate, and called to Zhao; Zhao pleaded grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu went out himself, passed Zhao's gate, and called to him; Zhao pleaded grave illness.

sentences.zh: 吳主燒其門，欲以恐之，昭亦不出。

translations.literal: The King of Wu burned his gate, intending to frighten him; Zhao still did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu set fire to his gate to frighten him; Zhao still would not emerge.

sentences.zh: 吳主使人滅火，住門良久。

translations.literal: The King of Wu had men extinguish the fire and stood at the gate a long while.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu had the fire put out and waited at the gate a long while.

sentences.zh: 昭諸子共扶昭起，吳主載以還宮，深自克責。

translations.literal: Zhao's sons together helped Zhao rise; the King of Wu carried him back to the palace and deeply blamed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's sons helped him up together; the King of Wu carried him back to the palace and reproached himself deeply.

sentences.zh: 昭不得已，然後朝會。

translations.literal: Zhao had no choice, and thereafter attended court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao could not refuse, and thereafter returned to court.

sentences.zh: 初，張彌、許晏等至襄平，公孫淵欲圖之，乃先分散其吏兵，中使秦旦、張群、杜德、黃強等及吏兵六十人置玄菟。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Mi, Xu Yan, and the rest reached Xiangping, Gongsun Yuan intended to plot against them and first dispersed their officials and troops, placing Palace Agents Qin Dan, Zhang Qun, Du De, Huang Qiang, and the rest with sixty officials and soldiers in Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Mi, Xu Yan, and their party reached Xiangping, Gongsun Yuan planned against them and first dispersed their officials and troops, placing palace agents Qin Dan, Zhang Qun, Du De, Huang Qiang, and sixty officials and soldiers in Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 玄菟在遼東北二百里，太守王贊，領戶二百，旦等皆捨於民家，仰其飲食，積四十許日。

translations.literal: Xuantu lay two hundred li northeast of Liaodong; Prefect Wang Zan governed two hundred households; Dan and the rest were all lodged with common families, relying on them for food and drink, for some forty-odd days.
translations.idiomatic: Xuantu lay two hundred li northeast of Liaodong; Prefect Wang Zan governed two hundred households; Dan and the others were lodged with common families and lived on their charity for some forty days.

sentences.zh: 旦與群等議曰：「吾人遠辱國命，自棄於此，與死無異。

translations.literal: Dan and Qun and the rest discussed, saying: "We have come far and disgraced the state's command, abandoning ourselves here—it is no different from death.
translations.idiomatic: Dan and Qun and the others discussed among themselves, saying, "We have come far and disgraced our state's command, abandoned in this place—we are as good as dead.

sentences.zh: 今觀此郡，形勢甚弱，若一旦同心，焚燒城郭，殺其長吏，為國報恥，然後伏死，足以無恨。

translations.literal: Now observing this commandery, its strength is very weak; if we once unite in heart, burn the walls and towns, and kill its chief officials to avenge the state, then willingly die—we will be without regret.
translations.idiomatic: This commandery is very weak; if we unite at once, burn its towns, kill its officials to avenge our state, and then accept death, we shall have no regret.

sentences.zh: 孰與偷生苟活，長為囚虜乎！

translations.literal: How does that compare with clinging to life in cowardice and long being prisoners!"
translations.idiomatic: How is that worse than clinging to life and remaining captives forever!"

sentences.zh: 」群等然之。

translations.literal: " Qun and the rest approved.
translations.idiomatic: Qun and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是陰相結約，當用八月十九日夜發。

translations.literal: Thereupon they secretly made a pact to rise on the night of the nineteenth of the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: They secretly agreed to rise on the night of the nineteenth of the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 其日中時，為郡中張松所告，贊便會士眾，閉城門，旦、群、德、強皆逾城得走。

translations.literal: At midday that day they were reported by Zhang Song of the commandery; Zan at once gathered the warriors, closed the city gate; Dan, Qun, De, and Qiang all climbed the wall and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At noon that day Zhang Song of the commandery reported them; Zan gathered his men and shut the gates; Dan, Qun, De, and Qiang climbed the walls and fled.

sentences.zh: 時群病疽創著膝，不及輩旅，德常扶接與俱，崎嶇山谷，行六七百里，創益困，不復能前，臥草中，相守悲泣。

translations.literal: At the time Qun was ill with a carbuncle wound on the knee and could not keep pace with the company; De often supported and accompanied him, over rugged mountains and valleys for six or seven hundred li; the wound grew worse and he could advance no further, lying in the grass, guarding each other and weeping in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was ill with a carbuncle on his knee and could not keep up; De often supported him through rugged hills for six or seven hundred li until the wound worsened and he could go no farther; they lay in the grass, guarding each other and weeping.

sentences.zh: 群曰：「吾不幸創甚，死亡無日，卿諸人宜速進道，冀有所達，空相守俱死於窮谷之中，何益也！

translations.literal: Qun said: "I am unlucky—my wound is severe and death is not far off; you gentlemen should hurry on the road and hope to reach safety; to guard each other and die together in this desolate valley—what good is it!"
translations.idiomatic: Qun said, "My wound is grave and death near; you should hurry on and hope to get through; to stay and die together in this ravine—what good is that!"

sentences.zh: 」德曰：「萬里流離，死生共之，不忍相委。

translations.literal: De said: "Ten thousand li from home, life and death shared—we cannot bear to leave you."
translations.idiomatic: De said, "We have wandered ten thousand li from home and share life and death—we cannot abandon you."

sentences.zh: 」於是推旦、強使前，德獨留守群，采菜果食之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they pushed Dan and Qiang to go ahead; De alone remained to guard Qun, gathering vegetables and fruit to eat.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed Dan and Qiang onward; De alone stayed with Qun, gathering wild plants to eat.

sentences.zh: 旦、強別數日，得達句麗，因宣吳主詔於句麗王位宮及其主簿，紿言有賜，為遼東所劫奪。

translations.literal: Dan and Qiang parted for several days and reached Goguryeo; they there proclaimed the King of Wu's edict to Goguryeo's king Weigong and his registrar, falsely saying there were gifts that Liaodong had robbed.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Dan and Qiang reached Goguryeo and proclaimed the King of Wu's edict to King Weigong and his registrar, falsely claiming that gifts had been seized by Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 位宮等大喜，即受詔，命使人隨旦還迎群、〔德〕<ref>命使人隨旦還迎群〔德〕據章注及《吳志．孫權傳》注引《吳書》補。

translations.literal: Weigong and the rest were greatly pleased and at once received the edict, ordering men to follow Dan back to welcome Qun and [De]<ref>ordering men to follow Dan back to welcome Qun [De] supplied according to Zhang's commentary and the note to the Biography of Sun Quan in the History of Wu citing the Book of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong and his court were delighted and received the edict at once, ordering men to follow Dan back to welcome Qun and [De]<ref>Supplied according to Zhang's commentary and the note to the Biography of Sun Quan in the History of Wu citing the Book of Wu.

sentences.zh: </ref>，遣皁衣二十五人，送旦等還吳，奉表稱臣，貢貂皮千枚，鶡雞皮十具。

translations.literal: </ref>, sending twenty-five men in black robes to escort Dan and the rest back to Wu, presenting a memorial declaring themselves subjects and offering a thousand sable pelts and ten suits of hawk-skin.
translations.idiomatic: [End editorial note.] They sent twenty-five men in black robes to escort Dan and the others back to Wu, with a memorial declaring subjection and tribute of a thousand sable pelts and ten suits of hawk-skin.

sentences.zh: 旦等見吳主，悲喜不能自勝。

translations.literal: When Dan and the rest saw the King of Wu, joy and grief overcame them beyond their own control.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan and the others saw the King of Wu, joy and grief overwhelmed them beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 吳主壯之，皆拜校尉。

translations.literal: The King of Wu praised their valor and all were appointed Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu praised their courage and appointed them all Commandants.

sentences.zh: 8是歲，吳主出兵欲圍新城，以其遠水，積二十餘日，不敢下船。

translations.literal: 8. This year the King of Wu marched out intending to besiege Xincheng; because the water was distant, for more than twenty days he did not dare disembark.
translations.idiomatic: 8. That year the King of Wu marched out intending to besiege Xincheng; the crossing was long and for more than twenty days he dared not land.

sentences.zh: 滿寵謂諸將曰：「孫權得吾移城，必於其眾中有自大之言。

translations.literal: Man Chong said to the generals: "Sun Quan, learning that we moved the city, will surely boast among his host.
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong told his generals, "Sun Quan, learning that we shifted the city, will surely boast to his troops.

sentences.zh: 今大舉來，欲要一切之功，雖不敢至，必當上岸耀兵以示有餘。

translations.literal: Coming in force now, he wants to seize a complete victory at one stroke; though he may not dare come all the way, he will surely land and display his troops to show he has surplus strength.
translations.idiomatic: He comes in force seeking a single decisive stroke; though he may not dare come all the way, he will surely land and parade his troops to show he has strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 」乃潛遣步騎六千，伏肥水隱處以待之。

translations.literal: " He secretly sent six thousand infantry and cavalry to lie in ambush along the Fei River in a hidden place to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly posted six thousand infantry and cavalry in ambush along the Fei River to await them.

sentences.zh: 吳主果上岸耀兵，寵伏軍卒起擊之，斬首數百，或有赴水死者。

translations.literal: The King of Wu did land and display his troops; Chong's hidden troops rose and struck, beheading several hundred, some drowning as they rushed into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu did land and parade his troops; Chong's ambush rose and struck, beheading several hundred, some drowning as they fled into the water.

sentences.zh: 吳主又使全綜攻六安，亦不克。

translations.literal: The King of Wu also sent Quan Zong to attack Liu'an, but he too did not overcome it.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu also sent Quan Zong to attack Liu'an, but he too failed.

translations.literal: Director of Laijiang Zhang Yi—here Sima Guang did not change "Shu" to "Han" but emended directly.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: In the title Director of Laijiang Zhang Yi, Sima Guang had not changed "Shu" to "Han" but emended the text directly.
