translations.literal: </ref>, enforced the law harshly; the southern Yi chieftain Liu Zhou rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: [End editorial note.] He enforced the law harshly, and the southern Yi chieftain Liu Zhou rebelled.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮以參軍巴西馬忠代翼，召翼令還。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang appointed Staff Officer Ma Zhong of Baxi to replace Yi and summoned Yi to return.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhuge Liang appointed Staff Officer Ma Zhong of Baxi to replace Yi and summoned Yi back.

sentences.zh: 其人謂翼宜速歸即罪。

translations.literal: The people told Yi he should hurry back and accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: People told Yi he should hurry back and accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 翼曰：「不然，吾以蠻夷蠢動，不稱職，故還耳。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Not so—I return because the barbarians stirred in folly and I was not equal to my post.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Not so—I return because the barbarians stirred in folly and I was not equal to my post.

sentences.zh: 然代人未至，吾方臨戰場，當運糧積穀，為滅賊之資，豈可以黜退之故而廢公家之務乎！

translations.literal: Yet my replacement has not arrived; I am still on the battlefield and ought to transport grain and accumulate stores as resources for destroying the enemy—how could I abandon the state's business because of dismissal and recall!
translations.idiomatic: But my replacement has not yet arrived. I am still at the front and ought to move grain and build up stores for destroying the enemy. How could I abandon the state's business just because I have been dismissed and recalled!

sentences.zh: 」於是統攝不懈，代到乃發。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he directed affairs tirelessly; only when his replacement arrived did he depart.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed on without slackening his command; only when his replacement arrived did he set out.

sentences.zh: 馬忠因其成基，破冑，斬之。

translations.literal: Ma Zhong, building on the foundation Yi had laid, defeated Gou and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhong built on the groundwork Zhang Yi had laid, defeated Liu Gou, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 10諸葛亮勸農講武，作木牛、流馬，運米集斜谷口，治斜谷邸閣；

translations.literal: 10 Zhuge Liang encouraged farming and drilled the troops, made wooden oxen and flowing horses, transported grain to gather at Xiegu mouth, and built granary lodges at Xiegu;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang encouraged agriculture and military training, devised the wooden ox and the flowing horse, hauled grain to stock the mouth of the Xie Valley, and built granaries there;

sentences.zh: 息民休士，三年而後用之。

translations.literal: he let the people rest and the soldiers recover, and after three years would employ them.
translations.idiomatic: he let the people and the troops recover, and only after three years put them to use.

sentences.zh: 1春，二月，亮悉大眾十萬由斜谷入寇，遣使約吳同時大舉。

translations.literal: 1 Spring, second month: Liang led his full force of one hundred thousand through Xiegu to invade and sent envoys to arrange a simultaneous great offensive with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, Zhuge Liang led his entire army of one hundred thousand through the Xie Valley to invade and sent envoys to coordinate a major simultaneous strike with Wu.

sentences.zh: 3三月，庚寅，山陽公卒，帝素服發喪。

translations.literal: 3 Third month, day Gengyin: the Duke of Shanyang died; the Emperor wore plain dress and proclaimed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day Gengyin, the Duke of Shanyang died; the emperor went into mourning dress and proclaimed the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 4己酉，大赦。

translations.literal: 4 Day Jiyou: general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiyou, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 4夏，四月，大疫。

translations.literal: 4 Summer, fourth month: great plague.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, a great epidemic broke out.

sentences.zh: 5崇華殿災。

translations.literal: 5 Chonghua Hall caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua Hall burned.

sentences.zh: 6諸葛亮至郿，軍於渭水之南。

translations.literal: 6 Zhuge Liang reached Mei and encamped south of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang reached Mei and encamped south of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 司馬懿引軍渡渭，背水為壘拒之，謂諸將曰：「亮若出武功，依山而東，誠為可憂；

translations.literal: Sima Yi led his army across the Wei, built fortifications with his back to the water to resist, and told the generals: "If Liang comes out through Wugong and marches east along the mountains, that would truly be worrisome;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi led his army across the Wei, built fortifications with the river at his back to hold them off, and told his generals, "If Liang comes out through Wugong and marches east along the mountains, that would be genuinely alarming;

sentences.zh: 若西上五丈原，諸將無事矣。

translations.literal: if he climbs west to Wuzhang Plains, you generals will have nothing to fear;
translations.idiomatic: if he climbs west to Wuzhang Plains, you generals will have nothing to fear;

sentences.zh: 」亮果屯五丈原。

translations.literal: " Liang indeed encamped at Wuzhang Plains.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang did indeed encamp at Wuzhang Plains.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史郭淮言於懿曰：「亮必爭北原，宜先據之。

translations.literal: Guo Huai, Inspector of Yong Province, said to Yi: "Liang is sure to contest the northern plain; we should seize it first."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai, Inspector of Yong Province, said to Sima Yi, "Liang is certain to fight for the northern plain—we should seize it first."

sentences.zh: 」議者多謂不然，淮曰：「若亮跨渭登原，連兵北山，隔絕隴道，搖蕩民夷，此非國之利也。

translations.literal: " Many in council said otherwise. Huai said: "If Liang crosses the Wei and gains the plain, links forces with Beishan, cuts the Long route, and stirs Han and Yi alike, that is no benefit to the state."
translations.idiomatic: " Most in council disagreed. Guo Huai said, "If Liang crosses the Wei and takes the plain, links with Beishan, severs the Long route, and stirs both Chinese settlers and tribal peoples, that will not serve the state."

sentences.zh: 」懿乃使淮屯北原。

translations.literal: " Yi then sent Huai to garrison the northern plain.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Yi then sent Guo Huai to hold the northern plain.

sentences.zh: 塹壘未成，漢兵大至，淮逆擊卻之。

translations.literal: Before trenches and ramparts were finished, Han troops arrived in force; Huai counterattacked and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Before the trenches and ramparts were finished, Han forces arrived in strength; Guo Huai counterattacked and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 亮以前者數出，皆以運糧不繼，使己志不伸，乃分兵屯田為久駐之基，耕者雜於渭濱居民之間，而百姓安堵，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: Liang, because his earlier expeditions had all failed for want of grain transport and his designs could not be fulfilled, now divided troops to open garrison farms as a basis for a long stay; the farmers mingled among the residents along the Wei banks, yet the common people were undisturbed and the army took nothing for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: Because his earlier campaigns had all stalled for lack of grain and his plans had never come to fruition, Liang now divided troops to farm garrison fields as a foundation for a long stay. The soldiers farming mingled among the people along the Wei, yet the locals lived in peace and the army took nothing for private gain.

sentences.zh: 7五月，吳主入居巢湖口，向合肥新城，眾號十萬；

translations.literal: 7 Fifth month: the Lord of Wu entered and encamped at Chaohu mouth, advanced on Hefei New City, forces claiming one hundred thousand;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Sun Quan moved into Chaohu mouth and advanced on Hefei New City at the head of forces said to number one hundred thousand;

sentences.zh: 又遣陸遜、諸葛瑾將萬餘人入江夏、沔口，向襄陽；

translations.literal: also sent Lu Xun and Zhuge Jin with more than ten thousand men into Jiangxia and Hankou toward Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: he also sent Lu Xun and Zhuge Jin with more than ten thousand men into Jiangxia and Hankou toward Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 將軍孫韶、張承入淮，向廣陵、淮陰。

translations.literal: Generals Sun Shao and Zhang Cheng entered the Huai toward Guangling and Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: and Generals Sun Shao and Zhang Cheng pushed into the Huai toward Guangling and Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 六月，滿寵欲率諸軍救新城，殄夷將軍田豫曰：「賊悉眾大舉，非圖小利，欲質新城以致大軍耳。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Man Chong wished to lead the armies to relieve New City. General Who Exterminates Barbarians Tian Yu said: "The bandits have thrown their full strength into the field—not after petty gain but to hold New City hostage to draw our main army."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Man Chong wanted to lead the armies to relieve New City. General Who Exterminates Barbarians Tian Yu said, "The enemy have committed their full strength—not for petty gain but to hold New City hostage and lure our main army."

sentences.zh: 宜聽使攻城，挫其銳氣，不當與爭鋒也。

translations.literal: We should let them besiege the city and blunt their edge—not meet them head on.
translations.idiomatic: We should let them besiege the city and blunt their fighting spirit—not meet them head-on.

sentences.zh: 城不可拔，眾必罷怠；

translations.literal: If the city cannot be taken, their masses are sure to weary and slacken;
translations.idiomatic: If they cannot take the city, their troops are sure to grow weary and slack;

sentences.zh: 罷怠然後擊之，可大克也。

translations.literal: when they are weary and slack, then strike—we can win a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: and once they are weary and slack, we can strike and win a great victory.

sentences.zh: 若賊見計，必不攻城，勢將自走。

translations.literal: If the bandits see through the plan, they will surely not besiege the city and will withdraw on their own.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy see through the plan, they will surely not besiege the city and will withdraw on their own.

sentences.zh: 若便進兵，適入其計矣。

translations.literal: If we advance troops at once, we fall straight into their trap."
translations.idiomatic: If we advance at once, we walk straight into their trap."

sentences.zh: 時東方吏士皆分休，寵表請召中軍兵，並召所休將士，須集擊之。

translations.literal: At that time the officials and soldiers of the east were all on furlough. Chong memorialized requesting the central army and all furloughed officers and men be summoned to muster for a strike.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the officials and soldiers of the east were all on leave. Man Chong memorialized asking that the central army be called up and all men on leave recalled to muster for an attack.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍廣平劉邵議以為：「賊眾新至，心專氣銳，寵以少人自戰其地，若便進擊，必不能制。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant Liu Shao of Guangping offered his view: "The bandits have just arrived, minds fixed and spirits sharp. Chong, with few men fighting on their own ground—if he attacks at once, he surely cannot control them."
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant Liu Shao of Guangping argued, "The enemy have just arrived, focused and sharp. Man Chong, with few men fighting on their own ground—if he attacks at once, he surely cannot control them."

sentences.zh: 寵請待兵，未有所失也，以為可先遣步兵五千，精騎三千，先軍前發，揚聲進道，震曜形勢。

translations.literal: Chong's request to await troops has not lost anything yet. It is thought one may first send five thousand foot and three thousand picked cavalry ahead of the main army, raising the cry of advance to dazzle the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong's request to wait for reinforcements has cost nothing. He proposes sending five thousand infantry and three thousand picked cavalry ahead of the main army, raising the cry of advance to overawe the enemy.

sentences.zh: 騎到合肥，疏其行隊，多其旌鼓，曜兵城下，引出賊後，擬其歸路，要其糧道。

translations.literal: When the cavalry reach Hefei, spread the column thin, multiply banners and drums, display troops below the walls, draw the enemy out behind them, aim at their return route, and threaten their grain route.
translations.idiomatic: When the cavalry reach Hefei, they should spread the column thin, multiply banners and drums, display troops below the walls, draw the enemy out behind them, threaten their line of retreat, and cut their grain route.

sentences.zh: 賊聞大軍來，騎斷其後，必震怖遁走，不戰自破矣。

translations.literal: When the bandits hear the great army is coming and cavalry cut their rear, they are sure to be shaken and flee in terror, breaking themselves without battle."
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy hear the great army is coming and cavalry cut their rear, they are sure to be shaken and flee in terror, defeating themselves without a fight."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted this plan.

sentences.zh: 寵欲拔新城守，致賊壽春，帝不聽，曰：「昔漢光武遣兵據略陽，終以破隗囂，先帝東置合肥，南守襄陽，西固祁山，賊來輒破於三城之下者，地有所必爭也。

translations.literal: Chong wished to abandon New City and lure the enemy to Shouchun. The Emperor would not hear it and said: "In olden days Emperor Guangwu sent troops to hold Lueyang and in the end broke Wei Xiao; the Former Emperor set Hefei in the east, guarded Xiangyang in the south, and secured Qishan in the west—whenever bandits came they were broken below these three cities, because the ground was ground they had to contest."
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong wanted to abandon New City and lure the enemy toward Shouchun. The emperor refused and said, "Long ago Emperor Guangwu of Han sent troops to hold Lueyang and in the end destroyed Wei Xiao; the Former Emperor placed Hefei in the east, guarded Xiangyang in the south, and secured Qishan in the west. Whenever bandits came they were broken below these three cities because the ground was ground they had to contest."

sentences.zh: 縱權攻新城，必不能拔。

translations.literal: Even if Quan attacks New City, he surely cannot take it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Sun Quan attacks New City, he surely cannot take it.

sentences.zh: 敕諸將堅守，吾將自往征之，比至，恐權走也。

translations.literal: Order the generals to hold firm. I shall campaign in person; by the time I arrive, I fear Quan will already have fled."
translations.idiomatic: Order the generals to hold firm. I shall campaign in person—by the time I arrive, I fear Sun Quan will already have fled."

sentences.zh: 」乃使征蜀護軍秦朗督步騎二萬助司馬懿御諸葛亮，敕懿：「但堅壁拒守以挫其鋒，彼進不得志，退無與戰，久停則糧盡，虜略無所獲，則必走；

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent Protector of the Army for the Shu Campaign Qin Lang to supervise twenty thousand foot and horse to aid Sima Yi against Zhuge Liang, charging Yi: "Only fortify and hold, resist to blunt their point. When they cannot advance to their wish and retreat with none to fight, a long halt will exhaust their grain; they will plunder nothing and must flee;
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent Protector of the Army for the Shu Campaign Qin Lang to command twenty thousand foot and horse to aid Sima Yi against Zhuge Liang, instructing Yi, "Only fortify and hold to blunt their edge. If they cannot advance to their wish and retreat with no one to fight, a long halt will exhaust their grain; they will plunder nothing and must flee;

sentences.zh: 走而追之，全勝之道也。

translations.literal: flee and pursue—that is the way to complete victory."
translations.idiomatic: flee—and then pursue. That is the way to complete victory."

sentences.zh: 」秋，七月，〔壬寅〕<ref>〔壬寅〕據章注及《魏志．明帝紀》補。

translations.literal: " Autumn, seventh month, [Renyin]<ref>[Renyin] supplied according to Zhang's annotations and the Annals of Mingdi in the History of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " In autumn, the seventh month, [Renyin]<ref>[Renyin] supplied according to Zhang's annotations and the Annals of Mingdi in the History of Wei.

sentences.zh: </ref>，帝御龍舟東征。

translations.literal: </ref>, the Emperor rode a dragon boat on an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> The emperor sailed east on a dragon boat to campaign.

sentences.zh: 滿寵募壯士焚吳攻具，射殺吳主之弟子泰；

translations.literal: Man Chong recruited stalwarts to burn Wu siege engines and shot dead the Lord of Wu's younger clansman Tai;
translations.idiomatic: Man Chong recruited stalwarts to burn Wu siege engines and shot dead Sun Quan's younger clansman Sun Tai;

sentences.zh: 又吳吏士多疾病。

translations.literal: moreover many Wu officers and soldiers were ill.
translations.idiomatic: and many Wu officers and soldiers fell ill.

sentences.zh: 帝未至數百里，疑兵先至。

translations.literal: The Emperor had not yet come within several hundred li when decoy troops arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor had come within several hundred li, decoy troops arrived first.

sentences.zh: 吳主始謂帝不能出，聞大軍至，遂遁，孫韶亦退。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu had first thought the Emperor could not come out; hearing the great army had arrived, he fled at once, and Sun Shao also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had first believed the emperor could not come out; when he heard the great army had arrived, he fled at once, and Sun Shao withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 陸遜遣親人韓扁奉表詣吳主，邏者得之。

translations.literal: Lu Xun sent a kinsman Han Bian to present a memorial to the Lord of Wu; scouts of the enemy seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun sent a kinsman, Han Bian, to present a memorial to Sun Quan; enemy scouts captured him.

sentences.zh: 諸葛瑾聞之甚懼，書與遜云：「大駕已還，賊得韓扁，具知吾闊狹，且水干，宜當急去。

translations.literal: Zhuge Jin heard and was greatly afraid; he wrote to Xun: "The imperial carriage has returned; the enemy got Han Bian and know our full situation, and the water is drying—we ought to withdraw at once."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jin was greatly alarmed when he heard and wrote to Lu Xun, "The imperial carriage has returned; the enemy captured Han Bian and know our full disposition, and the water is drying—we ought to withdraw at once."

sentences.zh: 」遜未答，方催人種葑、豆，與諸將弈棋、射戲如常。

translations.literal: " Xun did not answer but was urging men to plant turnips and beans and, with the generals, played chess and archery games as usual.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Xun did not reply but was urging men to plant turnips and beans and, with his generals, played chess and archery as usual.

sentences.zh: 瑾曰：「伯言多智略，其必當有以。

translations.literal: Jin said: "Boyan is full of stratagems; he must have some plan."
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "Boyan is full of stratagems—he must have some plan."

sentences.zh: 」乃自來見遜。

translations.literal: " He then came in person to see Xun.
translations.idiomatic: " He then came in person to see Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 遜曰：「賊知大駕已還，無所復憂，得專力於吾。

translations.literal: Xun said: "The enemy know the imperial carriage has returned and need fear nothing else; they can concentrate on us."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun said, "The enemy know the imperial carriage has returned and need fear nothing else—they can concentrate on us."

sentences.zh: 又已守要害之處，兵將意動，且當自定以安之，施設變術，然後出耳。

translations.literal: They already hold the vital points; officers and men are unsettled. We must first steady ourselves, lay stratagems, and only then withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: They already hold the vital points, and our officers and men are unsettled. We must first steady ourselves, lay stratagems, and only then withdraw.

sentences.zh: 今便示退，賊當謂吾怖，仍來相蹙，必敗之勢也。

translations.literal: If we show retreat now, the enemy will think we are afraid and will press us hard—a posture sure to bring defeat."
translations.idiomatic: If we show retreat now, the enemy will think we are afraid and will press us hard—a posture sure to bring defeat."

sentences.zh: 」乃密與瑾立計，令瑾督舟船，遜悉上兵馬以向襄陽城。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he secretly formed a plan with Jin: Jin was to command the boats while Xun led all troops and horses toward Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He then secretly formed a plan with Jin: Jin was to command the boats while Lu Xun led all troops and horses toward Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 魏人素憚遜名，遽還赴城。

translations.literal: The people of Wei had long feared Xun's name and hurried back to the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei forces had long feared Lu Xun's name and hurried back to the city.

sentences.zh: 瑾便引船出，遜徐整部伍，張拓聲勢，步趣船，魏人不敢逼。

translations.literal: Jin then led the boats out; Xun slowly reformed ranks, spread and inflated their posture, marched toward the boats—and the Wei men did not dare press them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then led the boats out; Lu Xun slowly reformed his ranks, inflated their posture, and marched toward the boats—and the Wei men did not dare press him.

sentences.zh: 行到白圍，託言往獵，潛遣將軍周峻、張梁等擊江夏、新市、安陸、石陽，斬獲千餘人而還。

translations.literal: Reaching Baiwei, he claimed to go hunting but secretly sent Generals Zhou Jun and Zhang Liang and others to strike Jiangxia, Xinshi, Anlu, and Shiyang, beheading and capturing more than a thousand before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Baiwei, he claimed to go hunting but secretly sent Generals Zhou Jun and Zhang Liang and others to strike Jiangxia, Xinshi, Anlu, and Shiyang, killing and capturing more than a thousand before returning.

sentences.zh: 群臣以為司馬懿方與諸葛亮相守未解，車駕可西幸長安。

translations.literal: The courtiers thought Sima Yi was still locked in stalemate with Zhuge Liang and the imperial carriage could proceed west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers thought Sima Yi was still locked in stalemate with Zhuge Liang and urged that the imperial carriage proceed west to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「權走，亮膽破，大軍足以制之，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Quan has fled; Liang's courage is broken—the great army is enough to control him. I have no worry."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Sun Quan has fled; Liang's courage is broken—the great army is enough to control him. I have no worry."

sentences.zh: 」遂進軍至壽春，錄諸將功，封賞各有差。

translations.literal: " He then advanced to Shouchun, recorded the generals' merits, and enfeoffed and rewarded each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: " He then advanced to Shouchun, recorded the generals' merits, and enfeoffed and rewarded each according to rank.

sentences.zh: 8八月，壬申，葬漢孝獻皇帝于禪陵。

translations.literal: 8 Eighth month, day Renshen: buried Emperor Xian of Han at Shan's Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day Renshen, Emperor Xian of Han was buried at Shan's Tomb.

sentences.zh: 9辛巳，帝還許昌。

translations.literal: 9 Day Xinsi: the Emperor returned to Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinsi, the emperor returned to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 10司馬懿與諸葛亮相守百餘日，亮數挑戰，懿不出。

translations.literal: 10 Sima Yi and Zhuge Liang faced each other for more than a hundred days. Liang repeatedly challenged him to battle; Yi did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi and Zhuge Liang faced each other for more than a hundred days. Liang repeatedly challenged him to battle; Yi would not come out.

sentences.zh: 亮乃遺懿巾幗婦人之服。

translations.literal: Liang then sent Yi women's headscarves and gowns.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then sent Yi women's headscarves and gowns.

sentences.zh: 懿怒，上表請戰，帝使衛尉辛毗杖節為軍師以制之。

translations.literal: Yi was enraged and memorialized requesting battle. The Emperor sent Director of the Guards Xin Pi with the staff of authority as army mentor to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was enraged and memorialized requesting battle. The emperor sent Director of the Guards Xin Pi with the staff of authority as army mentor to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 護軍姜維謂亮曰：「辛佐治杖節而到，賊不復出矣。

translations.literal: Protector of the Army Jiang Wei said to Liang: "Assistant Director Xin has come with the staff; the enemy will not come out again."
translations.idiomatic: Protector of the Army Jiang Wei said to Liang, "Assistant Director Xin has arrived with the staff—the enemy will not come out again."

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「彼本無戰情，所以固請戰者，以示武於其眾耳。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "They had no mind for battle from the start; they asked for battle only to show martial spirit to their masses."
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said, "They had no mind for battle from the start; they asked for battle only to show martial spirit to their troops."

sentences.zh: 將在軍，君命有所不受，苟能制吾，豈千里而請戰邪！

translations.literal: When the general is in the field, the sovereign's command is not always obeyed. If they could control me, would they ask for battle from a thousand li away?
translations.idiomatic: When the general is in the field, the sovereign's command is not always obeyed. If they could control me, would they ask for battle from a thousand li away?

sentences.zh: 亮遣使者至懿軍，懿問其寢食及事之煩簡，不問戎事。

translations.literal: Liang sent an envoy to Yi's camp. Yi asked about his eating and sleeping and how pressing his affairs were—not military matters.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent an envoy to Yi's camp. Yi asked about his eating and sleeping and how pressing his affairs were—not military matters.

sentences.zh: 使者對曰：「諸葛公夙興夜寐，罰二十已上，皆親覽焉；

translations.literal: The envoy replied: "Director Zhuge rises early and retires late; whenever the penalty is twenty lashes or more, he inspects it in person;
translations.idiomatic: The envoy replied, "Director Zhuge rises early and retires late; whenever the penalty is twenty lashes or more, he inspects it in person;

sentences.zh: 所啖食不至數升。

translations.literal: the food he eats does not amount to several sheng.
translations.idiomatic: the food he eats does not amount to several sheng.

sentences.zh: 」懿告人曰：「諸葛孔明食少事煩，其能久乎！

translations.literal: " Yi told others: "Zhuge Kongming eats little and has many affairs—how long can he last?
translations.idiomatic: " Yi told others, "Zhuge Kongming eats little and has many affairs—how long can he last?

sentences.zh: 亮病篤，漢〔主〕使尚書僕射李福省侍<ref>漢〔主〕使尚書僕射李福省侍據章注及《蜀志．楊宗傳》注引《益部耆舊雜記》補。

translations.literal: Liang's illness was grave; the Han [Lord] sent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Li Fu to attend his bedside<ref>The Han [Lord] sent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Li Fu to attend his bedside supplied according to Zhang's annotations and the note to the Biography of Yang Zong in the History of Shu citing the Miscellaneous Records of Elders of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's illness was grave; the Han [lord] sent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Li Fu to attend his bedside<ref>The Han [lord] sent Vice Director Li Fu to attend his bedside supplied according to Zhang's annotations and the note to the Biography of Yang Zong in the History of Shu citing the Miscellaneous Records of Elders of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: </ref>，因諮以國家大計。

translations.literal: </ref>, and consulted him on the great affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> and consulted him on the great affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 福至，與亮語已，別去，數日復還。

translations.literal: Fu arrived; when he had spoken with Liang he left, but returned after several days.
translations.idiomatic: Fu arrived; when he had finished speaking with Liang he left, but returned after several days.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「孤知君還意，近日言語雖彌日，有所不盡，更來亦決耳。

translations.literal: Liang said: "I know why you have come back. Though we talked many days lately, there was still something left unsaid—your return was already decided."
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "I know why you have come back. Though we talked for days lately, there was still something left unsaid—your return was already decided."

sentences.zh: 公所問者，公琰其宜也。

translations.literal: What you asked about—Gongyan is the fit man.
translations.idiomatic: As for what you asked—Gongyan is the right man.

sentences.zh: 」福謝：「前實失不咨請，如公百年後誰可任大事者，故輒還耳。

translations.literal: " Fu apologized: "Before I truly failed to ask—as at Your Excellency's death who could take the great affairs? So I came back."
translations.idiomatic: " Fu apologized, "Before, I truly failed to ask—as when Your Excellency passes on, who can take the great affairs? So I came back."

sentences.zh: 乞復請蔣琬之後，誰可任者？

translations.literal: I beg to ask again: after Jiang Wan, who can take the post?
translations.idiomatic: I beg to ask again: after Jiang Wan, who can take the post?

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「文偉可以繼之。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "Wenwei can succeed him."
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said, "Wenwei can succeed him."

sentences.zh: 」又問其次，亮不答。

translations.literal: " Asked again who next—Liang did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Asked who would come next, Liang did not answer.

sentences.zh: 是月，亮卒於軍中。

translations.literal: That month Liang died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liang died in the army.

sentences.zh: 長史楊儀整軍而出。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Yang Yi marshaled the army and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Yang Yi marshaled the army and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 百姓奔告司馬懿，懿追之。

translations.literal: The people ran to tell Sima Yi; Yi pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The people ran to tell Sima Yi, and Yi pursued.

sentences.zh: 姜維令儀反旗鳴鼓，若將向懿者，懿斂軍退，不敢逼。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei had Yi turn the flags and beat the drums as if about to strike Yi; Yi drew in his army and retreated, not daring to press.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei had Yang Yi turn the flags and beat the drums as if about to strike Yi; Yi drew in his army and retreated, not daring to press.

sentences.zh: 於是儀結陳而去，入谷然後發喪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi formed battle order and withdrew; only after entering the valley did they proclaim the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yang Yi formed battle order and withdrew; only after entering the valley did they proclaim the mourning.

sentences.zh: 百姓為之諺曰：「死諸葛走生仲達。

translations.literal: The people made a saying of it: "Dead Zhuge scares off living Zhongda."
translations.idiomatic: The people made a saying of it: "Dead Zhuge scares off living Zhongda."

sentences.zh: 」懿聞之，笑曰：「吾能料生，不能料死故也。

translations.literal: " Yi heard it and laughed: "I can gauge the living—I could not gauge the dead."
translations.idiomatic: " When Yi heard it, he laughed and said, "I can gauge the living—I could not gauge the dead."

sentences.zh: 」懿案行亮之營壘處所，歎曰：「天下奇才也！

translations.literal: " Yi inspected the sites of Liang's camps and works and sighed: "A rare genius under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: " Yi inspected the sites of Liang's camps and fortifications and sighed, "A rare genius under Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」追至赤岸，不及而還。

translations.literal: " He pursued to Red Bank but could not overtake and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: " He pursued to Red Bank but could not overtake them and turned back.

sentences.zh: 初，漢前軍師魏延，勇猛過人，善養士卒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Front Army Mentor Wei Yan surpassed others in fierceness and was skilled at nurturing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Front Army Mentor Wei Yan was fiercer than any other man and skilled at nurturing troops.

sentences.zh: 每隨亮出，輒欲請兵萬人，與亮異道會于潼關，如韓信故事，亮制而不許。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed Liang on campaign he wished to request ten thousand men and meet Liang by another route at Tong Pass, as in Han Xin's day—but Liang restrained him and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he followed Liang on campaign he wished to request ten thousand men and meet Liang by another route at Tong Pass, as Han Xin had done—but Liang restrained him and would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 延常謂亮為怯，嘆恨己才用之不盡。

translations.literal: Yan often said Liang was timid and lamented that his own talents were not fully used.
translations.idiomatic: Yan often called Liang timid and lamented that his own talents were not fully used.

sentences.zh: 楊儀為人幹敏，亮每出軍，儀常規畫分部，籌度糧穀，不稽思慮，斯須便了，軍戎節度，取辦於儀。

translations.literal: Yang Yi was capable and quick; whenever Liang took the field Yi would plan deployments and calculate grain stores without long deliberation—done in an instant—and military regulation drew on Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi was capable and quick; whenever Liang took the field Yi would plan deployments and calculate grain stores without long deliberation—done in an instant—and military regulation drew on Yi.

sentences.zh: 延性矜高，當時皆避下之，唯儀不假借延，延以為至忿，有如水火。

translations.literal: Yan was proud and overbearing; all at the time deferred to him except Yi, who would not indulge Yan—and Yan regarded this as the deepest resentment, like fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was proud and overbearing; everyone at the time deferred to him except Yi, who would not indulge him—and Yan regarded this as the deepest resentment, like fire and water.

sentences.zh: 亮深惜二人之才，不忍有所偏廢也。

translations.literal: Liang deeply prized both men's talents and could not bear to favor one and discard the other.
translations.idiomatic: Liang deeply prized both men's talents and could not bear to favor one and discard the other.

sentences.zh: 費禕使吳，吳主醉，問禕曰：「楊儀、魏延，牧豎小人也，雖嘗有鳴吠之益於時務，然既已任之，勢不得輕。

translations.literal: Fei Yi was sent to Wu; the Lord of Wu, drunk, asked Yi: "Yang Yi and Wei Yan are rustic petty men. Though they once barked to some benefit for the times, now that they are in post their station must not be slighted."
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi was sent to Wu; Sun Quan, drunk, asked Yi, "Yang Yi and Wei Yan are rustic petty men. Though they once barked to some benefit for the times, now that they are in post their station must not be slighted."

sentences.zh: 若一朝無諸葛亮，必為禍亂矣。

translations.literal: If one morning there were no Zhuge Liang, there would surely be calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhuge Liang were gone tomorrow, calamity and disorder would surely follow.

sentences.zh: 諸君憒憒，不知防慮於此，豈所謂貽厥孫謀乎！

translations.literal: You gentlemen are muddled and do not know to take precautions here—is this what is called securing blessing for one's descendants!
translations.idiomatic: You are all asleep at the switch, with no thought of guarding against this—what became of securing blessing for your descendants?

sentences.zh: 」禕對曰：「儀、延之不協，起於私忿耳，而無黥、韓難御之心也。

translations.literal: " Yi replied: "Yi and Yan's discord arises from private resentment alone, and they have no heart like Ying Bu and Han Xin, hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi replied, "The friction between Yi and Yan is nothing but private spite; neither harbors the unruliness of a Ying Bu or a Han Xin.

sentences.zh: 今方掃除強賊，混一函夏，功以才成，業由才廣，若捨此不任，防其後患，是猶備有風波而逆廢舟楫，非長計也。

translations.literal: Now we are just sweeping away powerful foes and unifying all within the seas; merit is accomplished through talent, enterprise is broadened through talent. If we set aside such men and do not employ them, guarding against later trouble, it is like preparing for wind and waves yet perversely abandoning boat and oar—not a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: We are in the midst of crushing our enemies and reuniting the realm; achievement rests on talent, and enterprise expands through talent. To cast such men aside and withhold office for fear of later trouble is like stocking for storms and then throwing away your boat—no strategy for the long haul.

sentences.zh: 亮病困，與儀及司馬費禕等作身歿之後退軍節度，令延斷後，姜維次之；

translations.literal: Liang, gravely ill, with Yi and Chief Clerk Fei Yi and others drew up regulations for withdrawing the army after his death, ordering Yan to bring up the rear and Jiang Wei next;
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, Liang worked out with Yang Yi, Chief Clerk Fei Yi, and others the plan for withdrawing after his death: Wei Yan was to cover the retreat, with Jiang Wei behind him;

sentences.zh: 若延或不從命，軍便自發。

translations.literal: If Yan perhaps did not obey orders, the army was to advance on its own.
translations.idiomatic: If Yan refused to obey, the army was to march on without him.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，儀秘不發喪，令禕往揣延意指。

translations.literal: When Liang died, Yi kept the death secret and did not announce mourning, sending Yi to sound out Yan's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang died, Yi concealed the news and sent Fei Yi to probe Wei Yan's intentions.

sentences.zh: 延曰：「丞相雖亡，吾自見在。

translations.literal: Yan said: "Though the Chancellor is gone, I myself am still here.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "The Chancellor may be dead, but I am still alive.

sentences.zh: 府親官屬，便可將喪還葬，吾當自率諸軍擊賊；

translations.literal: The Chancellor's close staff may take the coffin back for burial; I myself shall lead the armies to strike the foe;
translations.idiomatic: His staff may escort the coffin home for burial—I will lead the armies against the enemy myself;

sentences.zh: 云何以一人死廢天下之事邪！

translations.literal: How can one man's death be allowed to halt the affairs of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: how can the death of one man halt the affairs of the realm!

sentences.zh: 且魏延何人，當為楊儀之所部勒，作斷後將乎！

translations.literal: Besides, who is Wei Yan, that he should be commanded by Yang Yi and made rear-guard general!
translations.idiomatic: And who is Wei Yan, to take orders from Yang Yi as rear-guard general!

sentences.zh: 」自與禕共作行留部分，令禕手書與己連名，告下諸將。

translations.literal: " He himself with Yi jointly drew up the marching and staying dispositions, ordering Yi to write by hand and join names with him, and announce it to the generals below.
translations.idiomatic: " He drafted marching orders with Fei Yi, had Yi write them out and countersign, and sent them down to the generals.

sentences.zh: 禕紿延曰：「當為君還解楊長史。

translations.literal: Yi deceived Yan, saying: "I shall go back and settle matters with Chief Clerk Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi deceived Yan, saying, "I will go back and reason with Chief Clerk Yang.

sentences.zh: 長史文吏，稀更軍事，必不違命也。

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk is a civil clerk, rarely versed in military affairs, and will surely not disobey orders.
translations.idiomatic: He is a civil officer with little military experience—he will surely obey."

sentences.zh: 」禕出門，奔馬而去。

translations.literal: " Yi went out the gate and galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: Yi left the gate and galloped away.

sentences.zh: 延尋悔之，已不及矣。

translations.literal: Yan soon regretted it, but it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: Yan soon regretted it, but it was too late.

sentences.zh: 延使人覘儀等，欲案亮成規，諸營相次引軍還，延大怒，攙儀未發，率所領徑先南歸，所過燒絕閣道。

translations.literal: Yan sent men to spy on Yi and the rest, intending to follow Liang's settled plan; the camps in succession led their armies back. Yan was greatly angered, pushed ahead before Yi had set out, led his command straight south in advance, and wherever he passed burned and destroyed the plank roads.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent scouts to watch Yi and the others, intending to follow Liang's plan as the camps withdrew in turn. Furious, he marched out before Yi had moved, led his troops south ahead of the main body, and burned the plank roads wherever he passed.

sentences.zh: 延、儀各相表叛逆，一日之中，羽檄交至。

translations.literal: Yan and Yi each memorialized the other as rebel; within a single day urgent dispatches crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Yi each denounced the other as a traitor; within a day urgent dispatches flew back and forth.

sentences.zh: 漢主以問侍中董允、留府長史蔣琬，琬、允咸保儀而疑延。

translations.literal: The Han ruler asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Dong Yun and Chief Clerk of the Capital Residence Jiang Wan; Wan and Yun both vouched for Yi and suspected Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler consulted Dong Yun, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Jiang Wan, Chief Clerk left at the capital; both vouched for Yi and suspected Yan.

sentences.zh: 儀等令槎山通道，晝夜兼行，亦繼延後。

translations.literal: Yi and the rest ordered timbers cut to open a mountain path, marching day and night, and also followed in Yan's wake.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's party cut timbers to open a mountain road and marched day and night, pressing on Yan's heels.

sentences.zh: 延先至，據南谷口，遣兵逆擊儀等，儀等令將軍何平於前御延。

translations.literal: Yan arrived first, seized the Southern Valley Pass, and sent troops to strike Yi and the rest head-on; Yi and the rest ordered General He Ping to face Yan in front.
translations.idiomatic: Yan arrived first, seized the Southern Valley Pass, and sent troops to meet Yi head-on; Yi ordered General He Ping to block Yan.

sentences.zh: 平叱先登曰：「公亡，身尚未寒，汝輩何敢乃爾！

translations.literal: Ping shouted to those who charged first: "The lord is dead and his body not yet cold—how dare you act thus!
translations.idiomatic: Ping shouted to the vanguard: "Our lord is dead and his body not yet cold—how dare you behave like this!

sentences.zh: 」延士眾知曲在延，莫為用命，皆散。

translations.literal: " Yan's soldiers knew the wrong lay with Yan and none would fight for him; all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan's men knew the fault was his and would not fight; they scattered.

sentences.zh: 延獨與其子數人逃亡，奔漢中，儀遣將馬岱追斬之，遂夷延三族。

translations.literal: Yan alone with his son and a few men fled, running to Hanzhong; Yi sent the general Ma Dai in pursuit to behead him, and then exterminated Yan's clan to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: Yan fled to Hanzhong with only his son and a few followers; Yi sent Ma Dai in pursuit to behead him and exterminated his clan to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 蔣琬率宿衛諸營赴難北行，行數十里，延死問至，乃還。

translations.literal: Jiang Wan led the capital-guard camps north to the crisis; after marching several tens of li, word of Yan's death arrived, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan led the capital-guard camps north toward the crisis; after marching several tens of li, news of Yan's death arrived and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 始，延欲殺儀等，冀時論以己代諸葛輔政，故不北降魏而南還擊儀，實無反意也。

translations.literal: At the outset Yan had wished to kill Yi and the rest, hoping that public opinion would take him as Zhuge's successor in aiding governance; therefore he did not surrender north to Wei but returned south to strike Yi—he truly had no heart of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yan had meant to kill Yi and the rest, hoping opinion would make him Zhuge's successor; that is why he did not defect to Wei but marched south against Yi—he had no real intent to rebel.

sentences.zh: 諸軍還成都，大赦，謚諸葛亮曰忠武侯。

translations.literal: The armies returned to Chengdu; a general amnesty was proclaimed, and Zhuge Liang was given the posthumous title Loyal Martial Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The armies returned to Chengdu. A general amnesty was proclaimed, and Zhuge Liang was posthumously titled Loyal Martial Marquis.

sentences.zh: 初，亮表於漢主曰：「成都有桑八百株，薄田十五頃，子弟衣食自餘饒，臣不別治生以長尺寸。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liang had memorialized the Han ruler, saying: "In Chengdu I have eight hundred mulberry trees and fifteen qing of poor fields; my sons and younger brothers have food and clothing with surplus, and I do not separately manage livelihood to add an inch.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liang had told the Han ruler, "In Chengdu I have eight hundred mulberry trees and fifteen qing of thin fields—enough that my sons and brothers live with a modest surplus. I have not set up a separate household to grow my fortune.

sentences.zh: 若臣死之日，不使內有餘帛，外有贏財，以負陛下。

translations.literal: If on the day of my death there remain surplus silks within or surplus wealth without, I shall have failed Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If when I die there is surplus silk within or surplus wealth without, I will have failed Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」卒如其所言。

translations.literal: " At death it was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: At his death it was exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 丞相長史張裔常稱亮曰：「公賞不遺遠，罰不阿近，爵不可以無功取，刑不可以貴勢免，此賢愚之所以僉忘其身者也！

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Chancellor Zhang Yi often praised Liang, saying: "The lord rewards without overlooking the distant, punishes without favoring the near; rank cannot be taken without merit, punishment cannot be escaped through noble power—this is why worthy and foolish alike all forget themselves for him!
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Zhang Yi often said of Liang, "He rewards without overlooking the distant, punishes without favoring kin; rank cannot be taken without merit, and punishment cannot be bought with status—that is why worthy and simple alike give themselves wholly to him!

sentences.zh: ::陳壽評曰：諸葛亮之為相國也，撫百姓，示儀軌，約官職，從權制，開誠心，布公道；

translations.literal: Chen Shou's appraisal: In Zhuge Liang's service as Chancellor, he comforted the common people, displayed ritual norms, streamlined offices, followed expedient measures, opened sincere hearts, and spread impartial justice;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou remarked: As Chancellor, Zhuge Liang comforted the people, displayed ritual norms, streamlined offices, followed expedient measures, opened sincere hearts, and spread impartial justice;

sentences.zh: 盡忠益時者，雖讎必賞，犯治怠慢者，雖親必罰，服罪輸情者，雖重必釋，游辭巧飾者，雖輕必戮；

translations.literal: those who devoted loyalty to benefit the times, though enemies, were surely rewarded; those who violated governance through negligence, though kin, were surely punished; those who confessed guilt and yielded truth, though the crime was heavy, were surely released; those who roamed in words and adorned with craft, though the crime was light, were surely executed;
translations.idiomatic: those loyal in service were rewarded even if they had been enemies; those negligent in office were punished even if they were kin; those who confessed honestly were released even for grave offenses; those who wove excuses were executed even for light ones;

sentences.zh: 善無微而不賞，惡無纖而不貶；

translations.literal: good without the slightest went unrewarded, evil without the thinnest went undemoted;
translations.idiomatic: no good deed, however small, went unrewarded; no fault, however slight, went undisciplined;

sentences.zh: 庶事精練，物理其本，循名責實，虛偽不齒。

translations.literal: the hundred affairs were refined and practiced, things were governed at their root, names were pursued to verify reality, and the false were not ranked among them.
translations.idiomatic: affairs were handled with precision, causes traced to their roots, titles matched to deeds, and the insincere found no place.

sentences.zh: 終於邦域之內，鹹畏而愛之，刑政雖峻而無怨者，以其用心平而勸戒明也。

translations.literal: To the end within the realm all alike feared and loved him; though penal administration was severe there were none who resented—because his mind was level and his admonitions and warnings clear.
translations.idiomatic: Within the realm all feared and loved him alike; though punishments were stern, none bore resentment—because his heart was even and his warnings clear.

sentences.zh: 可謂識治之良才，管、蕭之亞匹矣！

translations.literal: He may be called a fine talent for recognizing governance, a near match to Guan Zhong and Xiao He!
translations.idiomatic: He may be called a master of governance, second only to Guan Zhong and Xiao He!

sentences.zh: 11初，長水校尉廖立，自謂才名宜為諸葛亮之副，常以職位游散，怏怏怨謗無已，亮廢立為民，徙之汶山。

translations.literal: 11. Earlier, Colonel of the Long Water Liao Li, considering his talent and fame fit to be Zhuge Liang's deputy, because his post was idle and wandering was constantly discontent, murmuring and slandering without end; Liang degraded Li to commoner status and exiled him to Wenshan.
translations.idiomatic: 11. Earlier, Colonel of the Long Water Liao Li had deemed his talent and reputation fit to make him Zhuge Liang's deputy; finding his post idle, he grumbled and slandered without cease. Liang stripped him of office and exiled him to Wenshan.

sentences.zh: 及亮卒，立垂泣曰：「吾終為左衽矣！

translations.literal: When Liang died, Li wept and said: "I am at last to wear the left lapel!
translations.idiomatic: When Liang died, Liao wept and said, "I am doomed to wear the barbarian lapel at last!

sentences.zh: 」李平聞之，亦發病死。

translations.literal: " Li Ping heard of it and also fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Ping heard of it and also fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 平常冀亮復收己，得自補復，策後人不能故也。

translations.literal: Ping had constantly hoped Liang would take him back in and he could restore himself; he had calculated that later men could not do so.
translations.idiomatic: Ping had long hoped Liang would take him back; he had reckoned that those who came after could not.

sentences.zh: ::習鑿齒論曰：昔管仲奪伯氏駢邑三百，沒齒而無怨言，聖人以為難。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi's discourse: In old times Guan Zhong took from Bo Shi three hundred households of Pian and to the end of his teeth there was no complaint—the sage considered that difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi wrote: Long ago Guan Zhong seized three hundred households of Pian from Bo Shi, and Bo Shi bore no complaint to his dying day—the sage deemed that difficult.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮之使廖立垂泣，李嚴致死，豈徒無怨言而已哉！

translations.literal: That Zhuge Liang could make Liao Li weep and Li Yan die—was it merely no complaint!
translations.idiomatic: That Zhuge Liang could bring Liao Li to tears and Li Yan to his death—was that merely bearing no complaint?

sentences.zh: 夫水至平而邪者取法，鑒至明而丑者忘怒；

translations.literal: Water when level and the crooked take it as model; a mirror when bright and the ugly forget anger;
translations.idiomatic: Water at its level gives the crooked their standard; a mirror at its brightness lets the ugly forget rage;

sentences.zh: 水鑒之所以能窮物而無怨者，以其無私也。

translations.literal: the reason water and mirror can exhaust things without resentment is that they are without selfishness.
translations.idiomatic: water and mirror can lay all things bare without breeding resentment because they are without selfishness.

sentences.zh: 水鑒無私，猶以免謗，況大人君子懷樂生之心，流矜恕之德，法行於不可不用，刑加乎自犯之罪，爵之而非私，誅之而不怒，天下有不服者乎！

translations.literal: Water and mirror without selfishness still escape slander—how much more when great men and gentlemen harbor a heart that delights in giving life, pour forth compassion and forgiveness, enact law where it cannot but be used, add punishment upon crimes one has committed oneself, bestow rank without private motive, execute without anger—would there be any under heaven who would not submit!
translations.idiomatic: Even water and mirror, though without selfishness, still escape slander—how much more when great men cherish life, extend compassion, enforce law only where it must be enforced, punish only self-incurred guilt, grant rank without favoritism, and execute without wrath: who under heaven would not submit?

translations.literal: The common people then according to the seasons privately sacrificed to him on the roads and paths; Colonel of Foot Soldiers Xi Long and others memorialized: "We ask to build a temple near his tomb at Mianyang and cut off private worship.
translations.idiomatic: The people then offered private seasonal sacrifices at crossroads; Colonel of Foot Soldiers Xi Long and others memorialized, "We ask to build a temple near his tomb at Mianyang and end private worship.

translations.literal: " The Han ruler followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han ruler agreed.

sentences.zh: 漢主以左將軍吳懿為車騎將軍，假節，督漢中；

translations.literal: The Han ruler appointed Left General Wu Yi General of Chariots and Cavalry, with acting staff, superintendent of Hanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler made Left General Wu Yi General of Chariots and Cavalry, with acting staff, to command Hanzhong;

sentences.zh: 以丞相長史蔣琬為尚書令，總統國事，尋加琬行都護，假節，領益州刺史。

translations.literal: he appointed Chief Clerk of the Chancellor Jiang Wan Director of the Masters of Writing, to preside over state affairs; soon he added to Wan Acting Protector-General, acting staff, and Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: he made Chief Clerk Jiang Wan Director of the Masters of Writing to oversee state affairs, and soon added Acting Protector-General with acting staff and governorship of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 時新喪元帥，遠近危悚，琬出類拔萃，處群僚之右，既無戚容，又無喜色，神守舉止，有如平日，由是眾望漸服。

translations.literal: At the time they had newly lost their supreme commander; far and near were alarmed and fearful. Wan stood out above the host of officials, placed to their right; he had neither a grieving countenance nor a joyful one—his spirit and bearing were as on ordinary days, and thereby the public hope gradually submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had just lost its commander; near and far were shaken. Wan stood out among the officials, yet showed neither grief nor elation—his bearing was as on any other day, and so the court gradually took heart.

sentences.zh: 吳人聞諸葛亮卒，恐魏承衰取〔漢〕(

translations.idiomatic: </ref> and reinforced Baqiu with ten thousand men—partly to stand ready to aid Han, partly to seize an opening for partition.

sentences.zh: 漢人聞之，亦增永安之守以防非常。

translations.literal: When the Han people heard of it, they also increased the garrison at Yong'an to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: When Han heard of it, they reinforced Yong'an against any surprise.

sentences.zh: 漢主使右中郎將宗預使吳，吳主問曰：「東之與西，譬猶一家，而聞西更增白帝之守，何也？

translations.literal: The Han ruler sent Right Gentleman-of-the-Interior Zong Yu on a mission to Wu; the Lord of Wu asked: "East and west are like one household—yet I hear the west has further strengthened the garrison at White Emperor City. Why?
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler sent Zong Yu, Right Gentleman-of-the-Interior, to Wu. Sun Quan asked, "East and west are one household—yet I hear you have strengthened White Emperor City. Why?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣以為東益巴丘之戍，西增白帝之守，皆事勢宜然，俱不足以相問也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your servant considers that the east increasing the garrison at Baqiu and the west increasing the garrison at White Emperor are both what the situation demands; neither is enough to question the other.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu replied, "I take it that your strengthening Baqiu and our strengthening White Emperor are both what circumstances require—neither is grounds for reproach.

sentences.zh: 」吳主大笑，嘉其抗盡，禮之亞於鄧芝。

translations.literal: " The Lord of Wu laughed greatly, praised his forthright exhaustiveness, and treated him with ceremony second only to Deng Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan laughed aloud, admired his blunt completeness, and honored him second only to Deng Zhi.

sentences.zh: 13吳諸葛恪以丹楊山險，民多果勁，雖前發兵，徒得外縣平民而已。

translations.literal: 13. Wu's Zhuge Ke, because Danyang's mountains were perilous and the people many and bold and resolute, though troops had been sent before had only obtained the commoners of outer counties.
translations.idiomatic: 13. In Wu, Zhuge Ke noted that Danyang's mountains were rugged and its people fierce; past campaigns had rounded up only the lowland commoners.

sentences.zh: 其餘深遠，莫能擒盡，屢自求為官出之，三年可得甲士四萬。

translations.literal: The rest in deep and distant places could not be captured to the end; he repeatedly asked to go out as an official to bring them in—in three years he could obtain forty thousand armored men.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the deep hills could not be taken; he repeatedly asked to go in person and in three years could raise forty thousand armored men.

sentences.zh: 眾議咸以為：「丹陽地勢險阻，與吳郡、會稽、新都、鄱陽四郡鄰接，周旋數十里，山谷萬重。

translations.literal: The assembled deliberation all considered: "Danyang's terrain is perilous and obstructed, bordering Wu, Kuaiji, Xindu, and Poyang—four commanderies—winding round several tens of li, valleys in ten thousand folds.
translations.idiomatic: The council argued: "Danyang is rugged, bordering Wu, Kuaiji, Xindu, and Poyang—hundreds of li of folded valleys.

sentences.zh: 其幽邃民人，未嘗入城邑，對長吏，皆仗兵野逸，白首於林莽；

translations.literal: Its secluded people had never entered walled towns; facing the chief officials, all bore arms and roamed wild, white-haired in forest and thicket;
translations.idiomatic: Its secluded inhabitants had never seen a walled town; they met officials armed and wild, white-haired in the woods;

sentences.zh: 逋亡宿惡，咸共逃竄。

translations.literal: fugitives and long-harbored villains all fled together.
translations.idiomatic: fugitives and hardened criminals fled together.

sentences.zh: 山出銅鐵，自鑄甲兵。

translations.literal: The mountains yielded copper and iron; they cast their own armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The hills yielded copper and iron, and they forged their own arms.

sentences.zh: 俗好武習戰，高尚氣力；

translations.literal: Their custom favored martial arts and practiced warfare, esteeming strength and spirit;
translations.idiomatic: They loved war and prized strength;

sentences.zh: 其升山赴險，抵突叢棘，若魚之走淵，猿狖之騰木也。

translations.literal: in climbing mountains and rushing perils, thrusting through thorn thickets, they were like fish fleeing the deep or gibbons leaping trees.
translations.idiomatic: climbing cliffs and charging through thorns, they moved like fish in a pool or apes in the trees.

sentences.zh: 時觀間隙，出為寇盜，每致兵征伐，尋其窟藏。

translations.literal: They watched for openings and went out as bandit raiders; whenever troops were sent to punish them, they sought their lairs and hiding places.
translations.idiomatic: They watched for openings to raid; whenever troops came, they vanished into their lairs.

sentences.zh: 其戰則蜂至，敗則鳥竄，自前世以來，不能羈也。

translations.literal: In battle they swarmed like bees; in defeat they scattered like birds—from former ages they could not be bridled.
translations.idiomatic: In battle they swarmed; in defeat they scattered like birds—no dynasty had ever bridled them.

sentences.zh: 」皆以為難。

translations.literal: " All considered it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: " All deemed it too hard.

sentences.zh: 恪父瑾聞之，亦以事終不逮，嘆曰：「恪不大興吾家，將赤吾族也！

translations.literal: Ke's father Jin heard of it and also considered the affair would in the end not succeed; he sighed: "If Ke does not greatly exalt our house, he will redden our clan!
translations.idiomatic: Ke's father Jin heard and judged the venture would fail; he sighed, "If Ke does not exalt our house, he will stain it red!

sentences.zh: 」恪盛陳其必捷，吳主乃拜恪為撫越將軍，領丹陽太守，使行其策。

translations.literal: " Ke strongly set forth that it would surely succeed; the Lord of Wu then appointed Ke General Who Pacifies the Yue, Administrator of Danyang, and had him carry out his plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Ke pressed that victory was certain; Sun Quan made him General Who Pacifies the Yue and Administrator of Danyang and let him try.

sentences.zh: 14冬，十一月，洛陽地震。

translations.literal: 14. Winter, eleventh month, Luoyang had an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: 14. In winter, the eleventh month, Luoyang was shaken by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 15吳潘濬討武陵蠻，數年，斬獲數萬。

translations.literal: 15. Wu's Pan Jun campaigned against the Wuling barbarians for several years and beheaded or captured tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: 15. In Wu, Pan Jun campaigned against the Wuling tribes for years, killing or capturing tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 自是群蠻衰弱，一方寧靜。

translations.literal: From this the barbarian groups weakened and the region was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes weakened thereafter and the region grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 十一月，濬還武昌。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Jun returned to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Jun returned to Wuchang.
